strategy_name: Bollinger band fade: buy lower band, sell middle band
mechanism: Price touching the statistical band (2 std devs) reverts toward the 20-session EMA; band breadth itself measures volatility state, so the trade only makes sense inside a range regime.
setup_summary: On BTCUSDT 1h: with Bollinger(20,2), buy when price touches the lower band and sell/exit when price returns to the middle band; sell when price reaches the upper band and buy to close at the middle band. The book notes that when price exceeds the highest average after a period of band narrowing, it 'is expected to level out', i.e. band touch in a narrowing-then-expanding regime flags exhaustion.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: close touches the outer band (or wick touches and the body stays inside). Invalidation: trend takeover — price rides the band / closes beyond it with band breadth expanding; then the band is a trend-persistence signal, not a reversion edge.
risk_geometry: entry on band-touch bar close; stop beyond the band edge (e.g., 1 ATR past the band); target the middle band; short expiry; still_valid = price remains inside the band envelope.
quote: a swing trader may buy when the low average is touched by price, and sell when the middle band is touched; or sell when price reaches the top and buy to close at the middle.
chapter_anchor: Part 4 Seg 1 (Bollinger Bands)
notes: Mean reversion against a trend is dangerous in 24/7 trending perps; the trade needs a range/regime filter (band persistence), which maps to V8's regime-filter concept. The book itself only frames this inside a range context. Falsifiable and cheap to screen on 1h data once a range regime filter exists.
book: Technical Analysis of Stock Trends Explained - An Easy-to-Understand System for Successful Trading 2013

strategy_name: Correlated exposure cap (same-dollar-direction pairs)
mechanism: Concurrent longs in two USD-correlated pairs (e.g., AUD/USD and NZD/USD) are one concentrated USD-direction bet, not diversification, because the USD is usually up or down against all majors on a given day
setup_summary: Before adding a second position, check correlation with existing exposure. Since the USD tends to be uniformly up or down across the majors, going long both AUD/USD and NZD/USD on simultaneous breakouts doubles the same underlying bet; treat it as one exposure or size down. Intentional concentration is acceptable only if deliberate.
trigger_invalidation: N/A - admission/risk rule rather than a signal; if one correlated leg collapses the other typically follows.
risk_geometry: N/A - gate at exposure admission: reject or aggregate the second correlated position; reduce size if the correlation is intentional.
quote: On most days, the U.S. dollar will be either up against all of the major currencies or down. The magnitude of the moves will be different... rather than being diversified, the exposure is highly concentrated, which creates a hidden risk in the positions.
chapter_anchor: Chapter 11, Mistake #3: Taking Highly Correlated Trades
notes: For V8: BTC and highly-correlated alt perps double up on the same macro/risk direction, so this extends the existing one-exposure-per-(instrument,direction) rule into a correlation-aware cap in RiskGate; correlation must be computed from PIT history, not live cross-asset data.
book: The Little Book of Currency Trading - How to Make Big Profits in the World of Forex 2010

strategy_name: Commodity-currency cross-market flow (gold/USD, oil/CAD/RUB, gold/AUD)
mechanism: commodity prices drive trade balances and flows of commodity-exporter economies, creating persistent cross-asset correlation regimes
setup_summary: Use commodity prices as a cross-market input for currency direction: rising gold => USD weakness (gold is the dollar's safe-haven alternative), AUD/CAD strength; rising oil => CAD and RUB strength, USD/CAD decline (gold breaking an important level is a tradeable signal for dollar-bloc proxies); the free-floating ruble tracks Brent 'in almost-perfect lockstep'.
trigger_invalidation: Correlations are regime-dependent; treat decoupling (e.g., gold up while USD up) as the invalidation signal for the pair.
risk_geometry: No entry geometry - a cross_market feature input to any expert; adds the cross_market feature group to the feature vocabulary.
quote: When Gold Goes Up, the USD Often Goes Down (and Vice Versa) ... the higher the oil prices are, the lower the USD/CAD value will be.
chapter_anchor: Section 06, Commodity currencies
notes: BTC is USD-priced but has no commodity-export mechanism, so the trade-balance transmission does not transfer; however DXY, gold, and equity risk-sentiment features are plausible regime inputs for BTC perps (risk-on/off) and worth testing as cross_market features. The 'almost-perfect lockstep' claim (RUB~Brent) is the strongest falsifiable correlation statement; Morgan Stanley's dollar+5% => oil -10 to -25% is an external citation, not the book's own data.
book: Forex Trading Basics & Secrets Volume 3.0

strategy_name: Mr. Market / margin of safety: buy at a large discount to intrinsic value, wait for reversion
setup_summary: Estimate intrinsic value per share; buy only when price trades at a large discount (the book's example: estimated value $70-72 vs purchase price $37, i.e. roughly half to 60% of value); expect Mr. Market to pay a fair price within 2-3 years as smart money, buybacks, or takeovers converge price to value. Short-term price swings (the 'wide range of prices' each year for GE/IBM/GM) are treated as Mr. Market's mood, not value changes.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: price drops to a pre-defined large discount to estimated value. Invalidation: the value estimate itself was wrong (earnings fade, business deteriorates), or price fails to converge to fair value after ~3 years - the book explicitly warns a bargain can 'remain a bargain forever (or worse)'.
risk_geometry: Entry at market when price < ~50-60% of estimated value; no price stop (margin of safety is the loss buffer); target = fair value; expiry = ~2-3 years (time-based reversion horizon); the smaller the discount, the closer to a no-trade.
quote: This means that if you buy shares at what you believe to be a bargain price and you are right, Mr. Market will eventually agree and offer to buy those shares at a fair price.
chapter_anchor: Ch.10 p.98 (framework in Ch.4 p.32-34)
notes: Requires an intrinsic-value anchor for BTC that the behavior-only feature stack cannot supply (the natural perp analog is a realized-cost-basis / MVRV-style floor, which is this book's mapping, not its text). The 2-3 year reversion claim is asserted, not tested in the book - the tested claim is the value factor's multi-year efficacy. 24/7 trading removes gap risk but not the slow reversion; leverage shortens the survivable horizon.
book: The Little Book That Beats the Market 2006

strategy_name: Evaluation-horizon gate: expect multi-year underperformance from a genuine edge; measure risk as long-run loss probability
setup_summary: A strategy with a real long-run edge still underperforms the market in 5 of every 12 months, in 1 of every 4 one-year windows, and in 1 of every 6 two-year windows; only on a 3-year horizon does the edge show (the Magic Formula beat the market in 160/169 three-year periods and was profitable in 169/169). Definition of risk: (1) probability of losing money long-term and (2) probability of underperforming alternatives long-term - not short-horizon volatility.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: any evidence-based claim about a strategy must use multi-year horizons before a verdict. Invalidation: a strategy judged failed on <3-year evidence may actually be a live edge mid-drawdown; conversely short-horizon outperformance is not evidence of edge.
risk_geometry: n/a - methodology for the lab/registry, not a tradable setup.
quote: Following the formula for any three-year period in a row, the magic formula beat the market averages 95 percent of the time
notes: Directly governs V8's registry gates (SCREENING -> REPLICATION -> SHADOW) and lab verdicts: demand frozen-OOS evidence spanning multiple years and expect months-to-years of underperformance from legitimate families. 'Magic formula did poorly for more than two years in a row in one of every six periods' (Ch.8) quantifies how long a false-failure window lasts. The 1h BTC frame only increases episode counts per calendar year - this does NOT shorten the horizon needed for an economic verdict.
book: The Little Book That Beats the Market 2006

strategy_name: Crowding-capacity persistence: edges survive because investors abandon them mid-drawdown and chase recent winners
setup_summary: A strategy's long-run edge persists partly because of human behavior: if it worked all the time, everyone would use it and the bargains would disappear, so genuine value strategies must have long lumpy underperformance stretches. Case studies: a bestselling author's formula fund underperformed 2 of its first 3 years (one year by 25%) then became a top fund; a disciplined manager lost most clients after 3-4 slow years then went on to trounce the market. Most investors switch to whatever worked in the past few years (performance chasing), which is exactly the wrong rotation point.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: evaluate a strategy's practical viability by its drawdown-tolerance requirement, not just its mean return. Invalidation: if adoption/crowding is high (edge widely followed), the edge decays toward zero even with correct execution.
risk_geometry: n/a - behavioral constraint on strategy selection and holding, not a tradable setup.
quote: if the magic formula worked all the time, everyone would probably use it. If everyone used it, it would probably stop working.
chapter_anchor: Ch.8 p.73 (Ch.8 p.71-72 fund/manager case studies; p.74 'most people look for a new strategy-usually one that has done well over the past few years')
notes: For V8: systematic, belief-independent execution is an advantage over human managers because it will not quit mid-drawdown (the registry, not the operator, decides). But the lesson cuts both ways: promotion criteria must include crowding/capacity monitoring, and naive rotation into recently-hot families (momentum in strategy space) is a known failure mode the lab should not encode as evidence.
book: The Little Book That Beats the Market 2006

strategy_name: Doji top-exhaustion (Northern doji at resistance)
mechanism: open equals close after an extended move shows balance/indecision; in an overbought rally the bulls can no longer sustain the highs, leaving the market 'tired' and vulnerable to a turn
setup_summary: After an extended/overbought rally (ideally after a tall white bar and/or at a prior resistance zone), a doji (open approx equal to close) forms. It is a top-exhaustion alert, most meaningful when doji are rare and when it confirms a resistance area. Action needs follow-through; a close above the doji's high (or the highest high of the doji and prior bar) invalidates.
trigger_invalidation: Close above the doji's high = 'bulls are refreshed', signal dead. Doji mid-range or inside a box range = no signal (no trend to reverse). Southern doji in a decline is weak unless it confirms a support level. Doji frequent on the chart = diminished significance.
risk_geometry: Entry: at confirmation (doji is an alert; book's worked example waits for follow-through). Stop: above the frozen doji/prior-bar high. Target: structure. Gravestone doji (open/low/close at session low) is the stronger top variant.
quote: When the market is rising and overbought, and then a doji appears after a tall, white candle, the Japanese say that the market is tired... A close over the doji's high could be a signal that the bulls have regained a foothold.
chapter_anchor: Ch2 S2 (pp.43-53), Ch4 (gravestone doji confirming box-top resistance, p.115)
notes: Doji are frequent on 1h crypto bars, and the book itself says doji lose meaning when common - so the family needs a rarity/context gate (confirm resistance, follow tall white bar, overbought). Clear invalidation semantics (close over the frozen high) fit V8's still_valid pattern.
book: The Candlestick Course 2003

strategy_name: 6/100 HV ratio volatility compression (mean reversion)
mechanism: Realized volatility is mean-reverting: when short-term (6-bar) HV drops below half of long-term (100-bar) HV, an outsized move is imminent (direction unknown)
setup_summary: Compute 6-bar and 100-bar historical volatilities (annualized stdev of log returns). When the 6/100 HV ratio drops below 0.50 while price consolidates, a large move is likely as volatility reverts to its mean; pair with a directional setup (pullback, TKO, DT-KO, micro pattern) to pick the side.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: 6/100 HV ratio <0.50 (volatility compression). The signal carries no direction - a directional expert must supply the side; if no setup forms, the signal is not tradeable. Exit when vol reverts / the directional setup completes.
risk_geometry: Filter/regime only; no entry/stop of its own. Book examples pair it with existing setups using the standard 5%-capped stops.
quote: when shorter term HV readings dropped below 50% of their longer-term HV readings, a large market move was prone to ensue as volatility reverts back to its mean.
chapter_anchor: Chapter 9, Finding Explosive Moves (pp. 111-121)
notes: Attributed to Connors & Hayward (Investment Secrets of a Hedge Fund Manager); the book stresses it does NOT predict direction. For V8 this is a volatility feature + regime filter that can gate or enrich directional families. Volatility mean reversion is strong in 24/7 crypto; on 1h the 6/100 windows map to 6 and 100 bars.
book: Dave Landry on Swing Trading 2001

strategy_name: Oscillator Swing System (3-10 oscillator stretch + open-to-close reversal)
mechanism: A five-bar stretch of the 3-10 price oscillator marks a short-term overbought/oversold extreme; the same-day open-to-close reversal confirms the snap back
setup_summary: On a market NOT in an ADX-confirmed opposite trend: when the 3-SMA-minus-10-SMA oscillator has 5 consecutive down days (oversold) and the market closes above its open, go long on the close; exit on the close 3-7 days later. Mirror for shorts after 5 consecutive up days and a close below the open.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: 5 consecutive oscillator-down days + close above open (long side). Invalidation: ADX>=30 with -DMI>+DMI (downtrend) prohibits longs; the 3-7 day close exit is mandatory. Book: short-side results much weaker than long side in the 1990-2000 bull regime.
risk_geometry: Entry: on the close of the signal day. Exit: fixed on the close 3-7 days later. Published backtest used no stops or money management.
quote: The 3-10 oscillator must have at least five consecutive down days. If the market closes above the open, go long on the close. Exit on the close three to seven days later.
chapter_anchor: Chapter 10, Market Timing for Swing Trading - Oscillator Swing System (pp. 129-132)
notes: Published 10-year S&P futures backtest: 143 trades, ~65% winners, profit factor 2.28 (long side much stronger - regime-dependent). The '5 consecutive days' stretch and open-to-close reversal are bar-based and executable on BTC 1h, but must be rescaled (5 bars vs 5 days) and frozen-registered. V8 currently has no active mean-reversion family, so this is a backlog candidate, not a formalization.
book: Dave Landry on Swing Trading 2001

strategy_name: CVR III-Modified (fear-index extreme reversal)
mechanism: An implied-volatility/fear index is mean-reverting; an extreme reading that begins to reverse intraday precedes a 3-7 day market reversal
setup_summary: For longs: the VIX low is above its 10-day MA, the VIX closes >=10% above its 10-day MA, and the VIX closes below its open -> buy the market on the close; exit on the close the day the VIX trades back below its prior 10-day MA (vol reversion). Mirror for shorts (VIX high below 10-day MA, close >=10% below, close above open).
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: all three VIX conditions on the same day. Invalidation: the fear index keeps extending away from its MA (no reversion); the exit event is itself the reversion to the 10-day MA.
risk_geometry: Entry: close of the signal day. Exit: close on the day the vol index reverts to its MA (typically 3-7 days). Published backtest used no stops.
quote: once the VIX was 10% or more away from its moving average, the stock market had a nearly 70% chance of reversing over the next three-to-seven days as the VIX returned to more average levels.
chapter_anchor: Chapter 10, Market Timing for Swing Trading - CVR III-Modified (pp. 138-141)
notes: Published backtest: 76% reversal accuracy over 3 days, profit factor 3.83 (long 84% / short 56%, bull-market biased). No VIX exists for BTCUSD; analogues are Deribit DVOL or funding-rate extremes, which sit outside current V8 data scope, and this is a market-level timing overlay that V8 keeps ABSENT by default under the complexity budget - hence DEFER_GATED. The mechanism is already partially captured by the realized-vol feature (finding NEW_volatility_mean_reversion).
book: Dave Landry on Swing Trading 2001

strategy_name: Multi-touch Chikou-peak / Kumo-shadow support-resistance levels
setup_summary: Draw horizontal levels through Chikou Span peaks (close-shifted-26): 2+ peaks touching one level = major S/R (author: often coincides with a Fibonacci retracement). Similarly, Kumo shadows (past clouds behind price) and flat Senkou B plateaus are major S/R; the longer the flat Senkou B, the stronger the level. A strong trend cannot occur until it breaks through the price of the shadow peak.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger = price approaches a 2+ touch level or shadow peak. Invalidation = clean close through the level; shadow weakens as price consolidates away from it. Zone map, not a standalone entry.
risk_geometry: No geometry; the level itself anchors entries/stops/targets for other strategies (e.g. alert placement below resistance for breakout entries).
quote: If you draw a horizontal line through a Chikou peak, it represents a support/resistance value. If you get many Chikou peaks hitting that horizontal line then it is a major support/resistance value. In most cases, if you get two or more peaks, this typically represents a Fibonacci value.
chapter_anchor: Chapter 1 'Chikou Span' (p.24); 'Kumo Cloud Components' (pp.35-39)
notes: Location-group feature: count of touches on a shifted-close-derived level is computable deterministically. On 1h BTC, 26-bar-shifted close levels may be noisier than in FX dailies (faster regime rotation), so treat as a candidate feature for zone-weighted S/R rather than a level to hard-trade. Useful as an anchor for alert placement in the ichimoku confluence family.
book: Trading with Ichimoku Clouds - The Essential Guide to Ichimoku Kinko Hyo Technical Analysis 2010

strategy_name: Consolidation / bracketing range trade
setup_summary: Chapter 11 (pp.175-186) is titled 'Consolidating, Bracketing, Accumulation, or Sideways Movement' and contains three explicitly numbered trading strategies (Strategy 1 p.178, Strategy 2 p.181, Strategy 3 p.183) plus 'Bull and Bear Traps'. The index references the 'trading range of, 181' and 'small trading range, 177'. Falsifiable: during bounded sideways movement, the range has definable boundaries that can be traded both directions.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: price within a defined horizontal range (consolidation). Invalidation: the range resolves directionally (trend resumes) or a trap produces a false break.
risk_geometry: Range-boundary entries; stop beyond the opposite range edge; the range top/bottom serve as both entry and exit references.
quote: Consolidation, 175-186
chapter_anchor: Index pp.175-186 (Ch.11 Consolidating, Bracketing, Accumulation, or Sideways Movement); p.181 'trading range of'
notes: Range/consolidation structure is observable on 1h BTC, but the three strategies' exact definitions live in Part 1; the 'trading range of' (p.181) suggests a range-width characterization usable as a volatility-compression feature.
book: The 10 Essentials of Forex Trading - The Rules for Turning Trading Patterns Into Profit 2007

strategy_name: Position before confirmation on slow-resolving tail theses (confirmation reprices the tail)
mechanism: For an event that is slow and uncertain to resolve, the moment the market acknowledges the possibility is the repricing event itself (Greek default insurance went 11bps to 2300bps); waiting for 'the whites of their eyes' means paying the already-expanded premium. Confidence is path-dependent: 'Once you lose confidence, you don't get it back.'
setup_summary: Methodology rule for tail/convexity theses: enter when the thesis is pre-registered and the premium is cheap, not after confirmation, because confirmation is the repricing event. Directly testable implication for V8: on deleveraging/cascade episodes, measure the entry-price gap between confirmation-gated triggers (e.g., first confirmed break after a crash) and thesis-first triggers (pre-registered level); the confirmation-gated entries are predicted to systematically overpay. Also: the position must survive chronology/timing error, since being wrong about ordering is the main residual risk.
trigger_invalidation: Residual risk is chronology, not outcome: 'My biggest fear. That I'm wrong about the chronology of events.' Being early is survivable only if sizing and carry cost allow it (2-3 year horizon at 11bps carry).
risk_geometry: Cost of early position (premium/carry while the thesis is unresolved) is the price of optionality; sizing must survive being early for years.
quote: Should I wait until I see the whites of their eyes before I position myself, or should I position myself now? The answer is now. Because the moment people think it is a possibility, it's expensive. ... Once you lose confidence, you don't get it back. You just don't.
chapter_anchor: Preface, 'The Biggest Short' (~18/396)
notes: The single most relevant methodology lesson for V8's backtest design: confirmation-gated candidate-episode entry is a systematic overpayment on tail events. Recommend an audit of how candidate entries are triggered against this bias. Direction NONE because it is an entry-timing/measurement lesson, not a side.
book: Boomerang - Travels in the New Third World 2012

strategy_name: Iron law of price-to-fundamental reversion (Kelly)
mechanism: A bubble is inflated by nothing firmer than expectations; once price untethers from its fundamental anchor, the deviation is not a new regime and the magnitude of the subsequent fall scales with the size of the deviation.
setup_summary: When an asset's price rises far above its fundamental anchor, the fall is proportional to the deviation. Kelly's falsifiable claim on housing: 'the more house prices rise relative to income and rents, the more they will subsequently fall' (predicted 40-50%, up to 66%, fall relative to income; price/earnings ratio above Google's). Crypto analog requiring an on-chain/value anchor: price-to-realized-price (MVRV-type) or price-to-miner-cost extremes as a reversion signal; perp price can be measured against the spot-anchored value.
trigger_invalidation: Reversion thesis invalid only if fundamentals actually grow into the price (Kelly: 'Where would this growth come from?' — the implied growth rate was implausible).
risk_geometry: No stop in the book; the documented failure mode for the short is being early — the deviation can keep widening for years before reverting, so the position is not time-boxed.
quote: There is an iron law of house prices: The more house prices rise relative to income and rents, the more they will subsequently fall.
chapter_anchor: Part III, 'Ireland's Original Sin' (Morgan Kelly section, ~186/396)
notes: A falsifiable statistical claim made in 2007 and borne out with unusual accuracy (documented in the book). For crypto there is no income/rent analog, but BTC has realized-price/hash-cost anchors; requires a value-anchor series not in the frozen feature vocabulary, hence backlog. The reversion is to an anchor, not to a rolling band.
book: Boomerang - Travels in the New Third World 2012

strategy_name: Crab / Deep Crab extension pattern - 1.618 XA projection with extreme BC
mechanism: an extreme 1.618 XA extension marks oversold/overbought exhaustion; the extreme price action into the zone signals the reversal
setup_summary: On BTCUSDT 1h: Crab - B <=0.618 retrace of XA, D at the exclusive 1.618 XA projection, extreme BC projection (typically 2.618/3.14/3.618; Deep Crab min 2.24), Alternate 1.27 or 1.618 AB=CD, C retrace 0.382-0.886. Deep Crab: B at 0.886 retracement, D still 1.618 XA projection. Book: Crab completions show the most extreme price action of all patterns and 'frequently experience sharp price action and dramatic reversals'.
trigger_invalidation: The 1.618 XA projection is the minimum completion requirement (BC projection convergence is the floor); slight overshoot of the 1.618 on the initial test is tolerated but the completion point should mark the turn; severe overshoot/continuation invalidates.
risk_geometry: IMPORTANT book-stated difference: extension patterns have no clean X-point stop reference ('the initial point (X) is a less significant point in the extension structure'), so stops are 'more subjective' and may require more risk than retracement patterns; wait for the 1.618 to be tested before entering.
quote: The Crab is a distinct 5-point extension structure that utilizes a 1.618 projection of the XA leg exclusively. This is the most critical aspect of the pattern and the defining level in the Potential Reversal Zone (PRZ).
chapter_anchor: Ch 7 'The Crab Pattern', pp. 121-148
notes: Deep Crab (0.886 B point, both B and X violated during CD leg) is explicitly a distinct pattern from Crab and Butterfly. Extension-pattern stop subjectivity is a risk-rule caveat for V8: a frozen X-ref stop does not exist here.
book: Harmonic Trading, Volume One - Profiting from the Natural Order of the Financial Markets 2010

strategy_name: Extreme-RSI reversal at significant intraday support/resistance (Bottom/Top Reversal)
setup_summary: On a 5m chart: at least 4-5 consecutive candles in one direction (extreme move), 5m RSI below 10 (bottom) or above 90 (top), price at or near a significant intraday support (bottom) or resistance (top) level, and an indecision candle (Doji/spinning top) or strong reversal candle at the extreme with high volume; enter on the first 1m or 5m candle making a new high (bottom) / new low (top).
trigger_invalidation: Trigger = new-high/new-low candle near the level after the extreme + indecision signal. Invalidation = price resumes the prior trend (new 5m low for longs); if price goes sideways/flat for a few minutes after entry, exit immediately (likely consolidation for another leg down); never catch a falling knife without confirmation.
risk_geometry: Entry = first 1m/5m candle to new high (long) or new low (short); stop = low of previous candle or low of day (long) / high of previous candle or high of day (short); target = next support/resistance level, or VWAP / 9 EMA / 20 EMA (whichever closer), or opposite-direction new 5m extreme; trail stop to break-even then to prior candle lows.
quote: The key to your success with Top and Bottom Reversals is trading the extremes at or near a significant daily support or resistance level.
chapter_anchor: Ch 7, Strategies 3 & 4 (Reversal Trading), lines 1242-1341
notes: Concrete and falsifiable (RSI threshold, candle-count, level proximity, entry candle). Crypto caveat: 24/7 liquidation cascades produce frequent RSI extremes on 1h bars, so the level-anchor and indecision-candle confirmation are load-bearing; without them the setup degenerates to catching falling knives. Mechanism sits adjacent to the DATA_BLOCKED capitulation backlog (capitulation_exhaustion) — proposed as a distinct exhaustion_reversal family anchored on location, not on volume climax.
book: How to Day Trade for a Living - Tools, Tactics, Money Management, Discipline and Trading Psychology 3rd edition

strategy_name: VWAP rejection/support trading (institutional anchor)
setup_summary: On a 5m chart, price action against the session VWAP: short when price tries but fails to break/close through VWAP (rejection) or when VWAP breaks and price closes below it; long when VWAP holds as support; enter as close to VWAP as possible; stop = 5m candle close through VWAP on the opposite side; target = next support/resistance level or previous day close.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger = VWAP rejection (short) or VWAP support hold (long), ideally with institutional flow visible. Invalidation = 5m candle close through VWAP (stop); if price trades sideways near VWAP (no institutional interest), stand aside.
risk_geometry: Entry at/near VWAP (minimize risk); stop = 5m close through VWAP; target = next level; sell half at target and move stop to break-even.
quote: I usually short stocks when traders try but fail to break the VWAP on 5-minute charts.
chapter_anchor: Ch 7, Strategy 6 (VWAP Trading), lines 1393-1424
notes: Mechanism claim: VWAP is the benchmark where institutional traders execute large orders, so failed attempts through it attract follow-on flow (self-fulfilling crowd). VWAP is directly computable on perp tapes (session-anchored or rolling); this is a strong new expert family candidate. The MOH worked example (short below VWAP, stop above VWAP, 1:3 R/R) is a clean falsifiable template.
book: How to Day Trade for a Living - Tools, Tactics, Money Management, Discipline and Trading Psychology 3rd edition

strategy_name: Horizontal support/resistance level trading
setup_summary: Draw horizontal S/R from DAILY-chart extreme wicks (not closes, not diagonal trendlines); levels are AREAS (5-10c band), validated by a clear prior bounce and by elevated volume near the level; on the intraday chart buy near support (long) or short near resistance (short), entering on an indecision candle at the level; stop = 5m candle close below support / above resistance; target = next level.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger = bounce at the level with volume and/or indecision candle. Invalidation = 5m close through the level; levels only count if they are near the current price range and have clear prior bounces.
risk_geometry: Entry as close to the level as possible; stop = 5m close through the level; target = next level (or half-dollar/round-dollar if none); sell half at target, move stop to break-even; short side mirrors with a close-above-resistance stop.
quote: Traders buy at support and sell at resistance, making their effectiveness a self-fulfilling prophecy.
chapter_anchor: Ch 7, Strategy 7 (Support or Resistance Trading), lines 1428-1486
notes: Strong new expert family candidate: frozen daily-wick extreme levels are deterministic (can be computed PIT from daily bars), and the level-as-area + close-through invalidation maps cleanly to frozen-ref + still_valid semantics. Book's methodological claim: the market 'remembers price levels' not trendlines; volume near the level confirms significance. KMX worked example provides exact level/target/stop structure.
book: How to Day Trade for a Living - Tools, Tactics, Money Management, Discipline and Trading Psychology 3rd edition

strategy_name: Red-to-Green / previous day close rotation
setup_summary: For a gapped/directional instrument: when price extends away from the previous day close and then moves back toward it with rising volume, trade the rotation — short from VWAP with target the previous day close (gapped-up case) or long toward the previous day close (gapped-down case); stop = nearest technical level (VWAP break or MA break); the move should work immediately.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger = high-volume move toward the previous day close from an extension. Invalidation = break of the nearest technical level (VWAP/MA); 'Red-to-Green moves should work immediately' — if price stalls, exit (implicit time-stop).
risk_geometry: Entry near VWAP or the anchoring level; stop = break of nearest technical level (VWAP/MA/support); target = previous day close; sell all at target, or bring stop to break-even once in profit.
quote: The previous day close is a powerful level of support or resistance and traders should trade toward it when there is rising volume.
chapter_anchor: Ch 7, Strategy 8 (Red-to-Green Trading), lines 1490-1516

strategy_name: Butterfly extension reversal
mechanism: a failed Gartley where D extends beyond X to the 1.272/1.618 expansion of XA marks an overbought/oversold extreme where a reversal becomes probable
setup_summary: Four legs X-A-B-C-D with D beyond X (the Gartley failure point) at the 1.272 or 1.618 expansion of XA; must contain a valid AB=CD within the AD swing; AB retraces .618/.786 (deeper first retracement is a clue). Countertrend entry at a major top/bottom. Negations: D beyond 2.618 of XA (trend continues), B beyond X, C beyond A, D not beyond X, or no internal AB=CD. Max risk is generally at the 1.618 level.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: D completes at 1.272/1.618 expansion of XA. Invalidated/negated: extension beyond 2.618 of XA; B above X (sell) or below X (buy); C beyond A; D fails to exceed X; gap toward completion is an overshoot warning.
risk_geometry: Entry: limit at D (1.272 or 1.618). Stop: just beyond the 1.618 expansion of XA (or fixed dollar amount if 1.618 too far - e.g., $500/contract euro). Targets: first .618 of AD, second 1.272 of AD; 3-part scale-outs used on reversals. Book warns failures are fast and violent - stops mandatory.
quote: The Butterfly pattern is best described as an extension pattern. It is also a failed Gartley pattern where the D completion point completes above the X.
chapter_anchor: Ch 6, Butterfly Pattern Description
notes: Contrarian top/bottom-picking at extremes is inherently high-risk with perp leverage ('when this one fails it usually fails in a big way'). No gaps in 24/7 markets removes one completion-side signal. Would need extra risk gating (heat cap, forced stop) and is a candidate for a later registry experiment, not an active expert.
book: Trade What You See - How To Profit from Pattern Recognition 2007

strategy_name: Opening Price Retracement day-trade setup
mechanism: the day's opening price acts as a magnet/decision anchor; a .618/.786 retracement of the off-open range in the direction of the open yields a high-probability intraday trade
setup_summary: Stocks only in the book. Price above the opening price 30-60 min after the open -> wait for a .618 or .786 retracement of the day's off-open range (low-to-high) and buy; below the open -> sell the .618/.786 retracement of the high-to-low off-open range. Only the current day's open is used. Claim: opening price sits in the upper/lower 20% of the day's range >60% of the time and price above (below) the open gives >60% long (short) win probability.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: .618/.786 retracement of the off-open range reached after an open-direction move. Invalidated/stand-aside: gap-through open with no retracement; warning signs (wide range bars); price consolidating sideways instead of moving to a retracement level.
risk_geometry: Entry: limit at .618/.786 of the off-open range. Stop: just below day low / above day high (e.g., 55c CTX, 85c GS). Target 1 = .618 of the first swing off entry, then move to breakeven; second target can use a forming pattern (e.g., Butterfly 1.27). Day trade - close flat by day end.
quote: if the price is above the opening price, the probability of a winning long trade is above 60 percent
chapter_anchor: Ch 8, Opening Price Retracement Setups
notes: The mechanism is tied to equity/futures session microstructure (overnight order accumulation around the auction open). 24/7 perps have no single auction; a UTC-day-open anchor could be tested but the '>60%' statistic is asserted, not demonstrated. Low-priority candidate; requires a session-anchor decision before any experiment.

strategy_name: Fibonacci retracement C-entry / D-extension (A-B-C-D wave)
mechanism: after an A->B rally the market retraces into the AB boundary and bounces at a Fibonacci retracement level; shallow retraces (0.382-0.618) imply strong follow-through to the 1.618 extension, while a deep 0.786 retrace implies weak follow-through to only the 1.27 extension
setup_summary: In an uptrend, take the latest A-B move, draw the Fibonacci retracement/extension grid, and enter long at the C bar close when price bounces at a 0.382/0.50/0.618 retracement, ideally at a convergence (Fib level + uptrend line + past support + bullish candle). Target the D extension (1.27 or 1.618) or the nearest of four past resistance levels, placing a limit exit 10 pips in front of the level. Mirror for downtrends.
trigger_invalidation: Invalid if price continues through the next Fib level without a bounce candle — retracement beyond 0.786 signals the trend is likely broken.
risk_geometry: Entry: bar close of the confirming bounce candle at the retracement level. Stop: sized by equity management (book's typical 30-50 pips) or beyond the C swing extreme. Target: D extension (1.27/1.618) or nearest of four past resistance/support levels, limit order 10 pips before the level; no explicit expiry.
quote: Should the market bounce at the 0.382, 0.50, or 0.618, it will predominately rally and go to a 1.618 extension... If it retraces all the way down to the 0.786, it will only go to the 1.27 extension.
chapter_anchor: Ch 8 'The Fibonacci Retracement and Extension Ratio Relationship' + 'Steps to Be Followed When Trading an Uptrend' (pp.140-149)
notes: The book's C-entry is explicitly a convergence stack (Fib + trend line + candlestick) — its cleanest articulation of 'multiple reasons to enter'. Fib levels are widely watched (self-fulfilling component). The shallow-vs-deep retrace-to-extension mapping is the falsifiable core. Fully implementable from OHLC alone.

strategy_name: Reversion to the mean of speculative return (valuation expansion compresses future returns)
mechanism: Total return = investment return (dividend yield + earnings growth) + speculative return (change in valuation multiple); speculative return is mean-reverting, so after large multiple expansion future returns are below the fundamental rate until valuation compresses back to the norm.
setup_summary: On a long dataset, when the valuation multiple (P/E; crypto analog: price vs realized-price/cost-basis anchor, funding premium) has expanded well above its long-run norm over the trailing N periods, forecast below-normal forward returns; when compressed, forecast above-normal. Every decade of significantly negative speculative return was immediately followed by a positive decade of correlative size (1910s-1920s, 1940s-1950s, 1970s-1980s).
trigger_invalidation: The pattern broke in the 1990s with a second consecutive expansion decade - reversion has no fixed clock; the book itself (Ch.7) uses it as a forward-return forecast tool, not a trade entry.
risk_geometry: No entry/stop; a regime overlay that reduces long exposure after large speculative expansion and restores it after contraction; horizon is decadal, far longer than V8's 1h-bar scale.
quote: Reversion to the mean (RTM) writ large.
chapter_anchor: Chapter 2 (Rational Exuberance, Exhibits 2.1-2.4), Chapter 7 (When the Good Times No Longer Roll)
notes: Crypto has no dividend/earnings anchor, so the analog is price-vs-realized-price (MVRV-type), funding premium, and cost-basis metrics; usable only as a regime filter at V8's horizon, not as a trade trigger.

strategy_name: Past performance does not persist: star funds revert and long streaks are luck on skill
mechanism: Performance RTM: fund returns are near-random across ranks; top-20 and #1 funds revert toward and below the peer mean the following year, and survivorship bias inflates apparent long-run records (223 of 355 funds from 1970 died; only 3 of 355 beat the S&P 500 by >1%/yr over 36 years).
setup_summary: Top-20 funds each year reverted to average rank the next year (avg follow-up rank 284/681 in 1982-92; 619/1,440 in 1995-2005), and the #1 funds reverted worst (avg 949/1,440, beating only 34% of peers). For V8: any backtested expert showing star performance must be stress-tested for RTM risk and survivorship bias before registry advancement; long streaks are 'extraordinary luck imposed on great skill'.
trigger_invalidation: Small samples cannot separate luck from skill - Aronson: 20-800 years of monitoring needed for 95% statistical confidence; Miller's 15-year streak shows rare skill can persist, so the rule is probabilistic, not deterministic.
risk_geometry: No trade geometry; a research-process rule: frozen OOS, registry gating, never promote on in-sample/backtest performance alone.
quote: In fund performance, the past is rarely prologue.
chapter_anchor: Chapter 8 (Selecting Long-Term Winners), Chapter 9 (Yesterday's Winners, Tomorrow's Losers)
notes: Applies directly to V8's own expert funnel (BACKLOG->FORMALIZED->SCREENING->...) and to crypto factor persistence, which decays faster than equity factor persistence.

strategy_name: Serious Money vs Funny Money: cap speculative allocation
mechanism: Speculative capital cap: at most ~5% of assets may go to speculation (funny money) while >=50-95% stays in a low-cost, low-turnover, diversified core, so that active or leveraged bets cannot destroy the portfolio regardless of outcome; the speculative sleeve is measured against the core at 1/5/10 years.
setup_summary: Allocate at most ~5% of capital to speculative/active/leveraged strategies and the rest to a passive diversified core; re-measure the two sleeves on fixed dates and compare. Falsifiable: over long windows the core is expected to win; if the speculative sleeve cannot beat the core net of costs, the cap is the binding constraint.
trigger_invalidation: If the speculative sleeve demonstrates verifiable positive net edge after costs and taxes, more than 5% may be justified; the cap is the default for unverified edge.
risk_geometry: Cap on total speculative capital, not per-trade R; per-trade risk still sized within the capped sleeve; maps to V8 heat cap in RiskGate.
quote: Not with one penny more than 5 percent of your investment assets. That can be your Funny Money account.
chapter_anchor: Chapter 18 (What Should I Do Now?)
notes: Perp leverage is the archetypal funny-money vehicle; the 5% cap is a practitioner heuristic that supports a strict heat/leverage cap in V8's RiskGate admission.

strategy_name: Broadest possible diversification: eliminate stock/style/manager risk, only market risk remains
mechanism: Diversification is the consummate risk-reduction strategy: holding the market in cap weights eliminates idiosyncratic, style and manager risk, leaving only undiversifiable market risk; concentrated or correlated bets retain exactly the risks that a diversified holder pays nothing to shed.
setup_summary: Any concentrated or correlated exposure set (a single perp, or several perps in one direction) retains idiosyncratic and correlation risk; risk gating should cap correlated exposure across instruments so no single name or style factor can dominate the book. The book's QED: individual businesses come and go via creative destruction, but the aggregate grows - only broad economic risk is undiversifiable.
trigger_invalidation: If a concentrated bet has verifiable, stable, cost-adjusted edge, concentration could be justified - exactly the claim the book says has been falsified for >99% of funds over 35+ years.
risk_geometry: Portfolio-level exposure limits, correlation-aware; aligns with V8 rule 16 (one active exposure per instrument-direction) and the correlated_exposure_cap risk rule.
quote: Owning businesses in the aggregate through an all-market index fund is the consummate risk-reduction strategy. (Broad economic risks to corporate earnings and dividends, however, cannot be diversified away.)
chapter_anchor: Chapter 17 (Relentless Rules, QED 2), Chapter 3 (Cast Your Lot with Business)
notes: Crypto is dominated by one factor (BTC beta), so naive diversification across alts is not diversification; the cap must be computed on realized correlation, not asset count.

strategy_name: Leveraged Carry Trade / Funding Carry
mechanism: Buying the high-yield currency and shorting the low-yield one harvests the interest differential plus appreciation; the trade profits only while risk appetite is high and unwinds violently when risk aversion spikes (carry unwind to safe havens).
setup_summary: Long the high-rate currency and short the low-rate currency (e.g., long AUD / short CHF, 4.50% yield pickup at zero leverage; 5x leverage makes it 22.5%). Profitability is conditional on the risk-appetite regime: profitable when investors have low risk aversion, unprofitable when risk aversion is high. Commit to a >=6-month horizon and avoid excessive leverage. Crypto analog: harvest funding on BTCUSDT perps (or long-basis carry); treat funding flips and risk-off spikes as the unwind trigger.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: persistent rate differential + risk-on regime. Invalidation: risk-aversion spike (credit event, crisis) - capital flows to safe-haven currencies and the carry turns sharply negative (book: yen +20% in two months in summer 1998; CHF +7% in 10 days after 9/11).
risk_geometry: Long-horizon (>=6 months) position; no tight stops (stops kill the carry); keep leverage low so fluctuations are survivable.
quote: Carry trades will generally be profitable when investors have low risk aversion, and unprofitable when investors have high risk aversion.
chapter_anchor: Ch. 9, 'Leveraged Carry Trade', p. 100-104
notes: Funding-rate carry and long-basis are directly implementable on Binance perps once funding data joins the tape; the risk-aversion dependence maps to crypto's funding/basis regime and flash-deleverage episodes (carry_unwind mechanism).

strategy_name: Currency Correlations Change Over Time (exposure management)
mechanism: Pairs/assets move together in time-varying correlations; 'diversified' portfolios of correlated instruments are actually concentrated, and correlation magnitudes/directions drift with economic regimes.
setup_summary: Compute rolling correlations over 1-month, 3-month, 6-month and 1-year windows (book examples: USD/CAD vs USD/JPY 0.06 at 1-month vs 0.80 at 1-year; GBP/USD vs AUD/USD -0.87 at 1-year flipping to +0.24 in early 2005). Treat two strongly correlated instruments as one position for exposure/heat purposes and recalculate at least monthly; do not take offsetting positions on correlated pairs as a hedge.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: correlation regime shift (typically interest-rate changes). Invalidation: correlation reverts to near zero - the exposure cap can loosen.
risk_geometry: No price geometry; portfolio-level exposure cap across correlated instruments.
quote: the most important aspect to remember when analyzing currency correlations is that they can easily change over time.
chapter_anchor: Ch. 6, 'What Are Currency Correlations and How Do Traders Use Them?', p. 56-60
notes: For BTCUSDT-focused V8 this is a cross-market exposure rule (BTC-ETH, BTC-risk-asset correlations), reinforcing correlated_exposure_cap with rolling-window correlation rather than static coefficients; most relevant when the instrument universe expands beyond a single perp.

strategy_name: Composite COT positioning extreme contrarian
mechanism: Errors of optimism/pessimism: speculators' net positioning peaks at tops and troughs at bottoms; commercials (hedgers) are the exact mirror, so their divergence quantifies where the crowd sits in the optimism-pessimism oscillation
setup_summary: Compute Composite COT = net speculative positioning - net commercial positioning on weekly data, then percentile-rank it over 52 weeks into a COT Index. A reading of 100 (specs extremely long / commercials extremely short) marks a bullish sentiment extreme; 0 marks a bearish extreme. Do not act on the index alone: filter with the speculative %-long ratio (long contracts / (long+short)), acting only when it is also extreme (above ~90% or below ~20%), i.e., when COT Index, Spec Ratio Index, and Comm Ratio Index all line up at 0 or 100.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: COT Index hits 0/100 AND spec %-long ratio is extreme (>90% or <10%). Thesis invalidated if price fails to turn within several weeks — extremes persist (May 2005 DXY: COT Index 100 held until July; book quotes Keynes 'the market can stay irrational longer than you can stay solvent'). Blind entry on the extreme alone produced poor results in Oct 2004 and May 2005.
risk_geometry: No explicit entry/stop/target; book says to keep risk tight and examine the chart for a reversal trade once the three indicators line up. Positioning data lags ~3-6 days (weekly report) so entries are delayed.
quote: Commercial positioning is on the wrong side of the market for the meat of the move but is correct at the turn.
chapter_anchor: Ch. 5, The Approach (Composite COT, COT Index, ratios), pp. 83-91
notes: Crypto analog is real-time funding rate + exchange open interest / long-short positioning, which has no weekly lag. Requires derivatives/positioning data beyond the base BTCUSDT tape; the 52-week percentile index must be computed point-in-time with a frozen window to avoid lookahead.

strategy_name: Pivot-point support/resistance with hit-rate statistics
mechanism: Pivot levels derived from the prior period's H/L/C are pre-planned reference points; measured hit rates let stops and targets be placed with known probabilities
setup_summary: Compute pivot = (H+L+C)/3 and S1/R1-S3/R3 from the previous period. EURUSD daily study Jan 1999-Oct 2006: the daily low averages 1 pip below S1 and pierces S1 44% of days; the daily high averages 1 pip below R1 and pierces R1 42% of days; S2/R2 pierced 17%, S3/R3 3%. Use these statistics to place stops below S1 (favorable odds) and take profits just below R1.
trigger_invalidation: Pivots are probabilities, not certainties; 'the high will exceed R1 4 days out of the next 10' is NOT implied by the 42% pierce rate. Hit rates are instrument-specific and must be re-measured per market.
risk_geometry: Stop: below S1 (long) / above R1 (short); target: just below R1 (long) / just above S1 (short).
quote: If you know that the pair slips below S1 44 percent of the time, then you can place a stop below S1 with confidence, knowing that probability is on your side.
chapter_anchor: Ch. 6, Pivot Points, pp. 112-114
notes: 24/7 crypto perp: pivots are computable on any fixed UTC period with no session-gap distortion; hit rates must be re-measured on BTCUSDT 1h. Supplies location features and empirically-grounded stop/target placement for risk_geometry.

strategy_name: Technical-Structure Stop Placement
mechanism: placing the stop at a technical reference (swing point, ATR band, Parabolic SAR) makes the stop distance a quantified risk measure rather than an arbitrary fixed amount
setup_summary: Each trade's stop is set at a level derived from technical analysis (support/resistance, ATR, chart structure per the book's indicator repertoire) so stop placement itself is the mechanism for quantifying and controlling risk.
trigger_invalidation: Invalid if the stop is placed at an arbitrary fixed percentage or pip amount unrelated to market structure.
risk_geometry: stop at technical reference; stop distance defines 1R; target set by the reward-to-risk target
quote: With regard to the analytical side of trading, technical analysis excels as a method for quantifying and controlling risk through stop loss placement.

strategy_name: Correlated-Exposure and Overload Cap
mechanism: overloading positions under leverage builds a nondiversified, highly correlated book where many small bets act as one large bet, so total exposure must be capped and sizing kept prudent
setup_summary: Total open exposure is capped to prevent margin overextension and concentrated, correlated positions; sizing is explicitly 'prudent' and avoids overloading, with diversification and pair correlation treated as risk controls.
trigger_invalidation: Invalid if exposure aggregation ignores correlation between simultaneously open positions; cap must be deterministic, not advisory.
risk_geometry: portfolio-level cap on total risk units/margin used; correlation-aware aggregation of open exposures

Overtrading in this respect carries the danger not only of margin overextension, but also potentially precarious exposure to a nondiversified, highly correlated portfolio of currency holdings.

strategy_name: Position-overload cap: limit concurrent positions because instruments are highly correlated
mechanism: Overtrading multiplies correlated exposure: the handful of tradable pairs all depend on the same underlying (USD, then EUR/JPY/GBP crosses), so holding many positions is not diversification; a strict cap on concurrent positions and per-position size reductions control this risk.
setup_summary: Impose a strict maximum on the number of concurrently open positions; when fewer instruments are tradable and they are closely correlated (all USD pairs, then crosses), additional positions mostly add correlated exposure rather than diversification. Reduce per-position size (multiple fractional positions) as an alternative to reducing count. The book rejects broker hedging and synthetic-pair quasi-hedging as risk controls (long EUR/USD + long USD/CHF == long EUR/CHF).
trigger_invalidation: N/A — risk rule limiting exposure concentration; no market trigger.
risk_geometry: Cap: max concurrent positions. Sizing: fractional positions (e.g. 10 mini-lots instead of 1 standard lot) so each unit can be scaled out at different prices. No stop geometry — this is an exposure-concentration constraint.
quote: The most obvious way is to place a strict maximum on the number of positions entered at one time.

In perp crypto the correlation argument is even stronger (altcoins co-move with BTC; venue-wide liquidation cascades); a strict concurrent-position cap plus aggregate-correlation guard is directly implementable in RiskGate. strategy_name: Extended Bollinger Band reversal
mechanism: price beyond the ~99% outer band is an extreme-value state; re-entry inside the band confirms the crowd has exhausted and a reversal follows
setup_summary: Use two band settings: standard (20, 2) capturing ~96% and an Extended Bollinger Band (13, 2.618) capturing ~99%. A strong sell signal occurs when price goes beyond the upper EBB then closes back below it; a strong buy signal when price goes beyond the lower EBB then closes back above it. Falsifiable on 1h: close beyond the (20,2.618) band followed by close inside predicts an N-bar reversal at better than base rate.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: close outside outer band then close back inside, direction opposite the extreme. Invalidation: price walks the band and keeps extending (book: don't assume price stops at a band - it can stay there); band ride without reclaim is not a signal.
risk_geometry: Entry: bar close back inside the outer band; stop = beyond the extreme (structure); target = middle band or 1R; expiry moderate; narrow-band condition is instead the breakout prelude (see volatility_breakout).
quote: If the price goes beyond the EBB and then returns below it, this is a strong sell signal. ... If the price goes beyond the bottom EBB and then returns above it, it is a strong buy signal!

notes: Cleanly implementable from ATR/std band math on 1h closes; the 'reclaim by close' structure matches V8's liquidity_sweep_reclaim style (frozen ref + close reclaim). Book also states price at extreme bands is a high-probability pause/reversal zone (p. 99).

strategy_name: Surprise-event shock, reaction, and retracement
mechanism: an exogenous surprise produces an immediate one-direction reaction, then the shock wave diffuses and price retraces toward pre-event levels, so the retracement leg is tradable
setup_summary: When a scheduled or surprise event (data release, central bank statement, geopolitical shock) drives a sharp one-direction move, do not chase the initial impulse; enter the opposite direction once the reaction stalls or visibly reverses, with an expiry covering the retracement. Book cases: Japan quake yen surge then BOJ-stopped bounce (4:1); Paris attacks gold spike then weekly decline; Ukraine Monday risk-off -> Friday risk-appetite. Falsifiable: for BTCUSDT, macro-shock candles (FOMC/CPI/NFP) with |return| > k*ATR are followed by a partial retracement (measurable mean reversion fraction) within N bars.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: large shock move (event candle > threshold ATR multiple) followed by stall/reversal bar. Invalidation: news creates genuinely new conditions and the move extends (book: 'if the news was so strong, it creates new conditions, and therefore, the price is likely not to reverse that quickly'); reversal fails and impulse resumes.
risk_geometry: Entry: bar close after reaction stalls; stop = beyond the shock extreme; target = 38.2-61.8% retracement of the shock move (fib-of-shock); expiry short-to-medium (book: hours to end-of-week).
quote: These events also have in common surprise followed by the reaction of the markets similar to a chemical reaction diffusion process. The markets react and then the initial shock wave is diffused out. It is in the reaction phase when binary option trading opportunities occur.
notes: BTC reacts to scheduled macro events and flash news; 24/7 markets and high leverage make stop placement critical. Requires an event-labeling layer (economic calendar + surprise magnitude) not currently in V8 - DEFER until calendar data is wired.

strategy_name: ATM (at-the-money) bounce / near-the-money mean reversion
mechanism: strike-anchored mean reversion: price that drifts to the at-the-money region tends to bounce because dealer/structural flows around the strike absorb extremes
setup_summary: Price trading near the at-the-money strike (for perp: a round number / prior-session anchor level) after a drift into overextension bounces back rather than continuing through; enter the bounce at the level with a tight invalidation. Book example: West Texas oil Jan-Feb 2011 bounce.

risk_geometry: Entry on bar close at/inside the anchor zone; stop beyond the level or 1 ATR; target ~1R back toward the prior range; expiry ~8 bars.

setup_summary: The book shows markets co-move on shared macro shocks and argues for choosing non-correlated trades to spread risk. strategy_name: ATR-multiple protective/trailing stop
mechanism: stop distance is scaled to volatility via average true range, and the stop ratchets up (long) using the highest-high of the stop value over a lookback so it can never loosen
setup_summary: Long: stop_line = close - AtrX*ATR(period) with example AtrX=1.3, period=13; take HHV(stop_line, 13) as the active stop so it ratchets. Exit when price closes below the stop line; for a long position a close above/at the stop line may also justify entry if other indicators support the trend. Falsifiable: in choppy regimes too-close ATR stops trigger early; in strong trends too-far stops fail to lock profit - the correct ATR multiple is regime-dependent.
trigger_invalidation: Trailing stop is always active; ratchet prevents loosening.
risk_geometry: Stop = close - ATR multiple, ratcheted via HHV lookback; exit on bar close below stop; stops act as last-resort exits ('protective stops').

strategy_name: The Pendulum (range-fraction mean reversion)
mechanism: Range price oscillates around a midpoint under a mean-restoring force; entering only after price has turned back 10% of the range from the extreme avoids catching a falling knife and gives objective 50%/90% exit zones.
setup_summary: On H1/H4, define a range from at least two confirmed support/resistance touches. Enter long when price bounces off support and has retraced 10% of the range back up (short when it turns 10% down from resistance); targets at the 50% and 90% marks of the range; stop at 1:1 R from entry. Example: AUD/USD H4, 269-pip range, enter 27 pips above support, targets 135 and 243 pips above support.
trigger_invalidation: Invalid if the range breaks before the 10% turn trigger fires (pendulum 'string snaps' - momentum wins); stop = 1:1 R; dead thesis if price closes through support/resistance.
risk_geometry: Entry at the 10%-of-range turn confirmation (market); stop at 1:1 R (e.g., 108 pips in example); targets at 50% and 90% of range; expiry: swing.
quote: We do this by executing a trade only at the 10% mark after prices turn back from either support or resistance. The first target is set at the 50% mark of the range, and the second target is set at the 90% mark of the range.

strategy_name: Gawk and Balk the Talk (Rule of 20 news-surprise trading)
mechanism: Traders price expectations, not prints; only a news surprise large enough to breach the forecast-error band (20% of the forecast, or 20bp for rates / 50bp for PMI) changes positioning, so price moves in the direction of the surprise.
setup_summary: On M15/M30 around the top scheduled macro releases (NFP, CPI, rate decisions, GDP, trade balance, PMI, retail sales), compare actual vs forecast. If actual exceeds forecast by >=20% (20bp rates / 50bp PMI), go long the affected currency pair (direction depends on whether the currency is base or counter); if actual falls short by >=20%, go short. Stop 20 pips, target 40 pips (1:2 R).
trigger_invalidation: No trade if the deviation is under the 20% threshold; stop 20 pips; trade only on the named high-impact releases (color-coded red flags on the economic calendar).
risk_geometry: Entry at the news-release candle (market, after the print); stop 20 pips; target 40 pips (1:2 R); expiry: intraday.

strategy_name: The Round Trip: fade extensions to round-number order clusters
mechanism: traders place entries, stops, and exits at round numbers, so order clusters pool at those levels (psychological support/resistance); each test consumes the pool - the first bounce is best - and once the pool is depleted the level finally breaks
setup_summary: On a 5/10/15-minute chart, price that had been tracking the 20-period MA suddenly runs at least 20 pips away from it toward a large round number (further extension = better setup). Enter long at the round number if price is falling toward it (short if rising); stop = 15 pips + spread from entry; first exit = 1R with stop moved to breakeven; second exit at prior support/resistance. Do not trade if the pair's spread exceeds 5 pips.
trigger_invalidation: Only trade a FRESH round-number bounce (first bounce best; each subsequent test diminishes the order pool and the odds); invalid if price closes through the round number; the 'no spread > 5 pips' constraint is a hard rule because every pip matters in a small playing field.
risk_geometry: Entry at round number via limit order; stop = 15 pips + spread; exit1 = +1R, stop to breakeven; exit2 = prior S/R level; fixed-pip geometry only valid for narrow-spread pairs; max hold is intraday (the move is 'swift and brief').
quote: The first bounce off of round number support or resistance is usually the best bounce... with each subsequent test, the pool of orders is diminished and the chances for a successful trade are decreased.

strategy_name: The Boomerang: fade low-volume breakouts in the FX dead zone
mechanism: in the thin window between the US close and the Asian open, orders too small to matter in normal volume can move the market; such moves are unreliable and likely to retrace to the opening price
setup_summary: EUR/USD only, just after 17:00 NY (after most market makers' interest rollover): place a sell order 15 pips above the 5-minute 'opening' price and a buy order 15 pips below it; stop 15 pips (1:1 risk-reward); target = the opening price; cancel BOTH orders if neither fills within 2 hours (before Asian volume arrives).

strategy_name: Rectangle Intra-Formation Range Trading
setup_summary: Within a tall, valid rectangle (>=2 peaks near the same price and >=2 valleys near the same price, i.e., >=4 printed touches), buy near the bottom trendline and sell/short near the top, with stops outside the rectangle; exit each leg at the opposite boundary. The book's example rectangle yielded 40% long / 29% short swings per leg. The author warns these are rare, for experienced traders, and that as soon as a pattern becomes repeatable it stops repeating.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: price reaches the bottom trendline inside a valid rectangle → long; the top trendline → short. Invalidation: a breakout close beyond either trendline ends the range (stop outside the rectangle triggers); a 'partial decline' near the top instead signals an imminent upward breakout (see partial_decline_breakout), which conflicts with the short leg.
risk_geometry: Entry: limit near the bottom/top trendline. Stop: outside the rectangle, far enough to survive normal price action. Target: the opposite trendline. Expiry: until a breakout close ends the pattern.

strategy_name: Size capital so every signal is tradable (participation breadth)
mechanism: Participation-breadth diversification: an account too small to take a signal filters it out, concentrating PnL on fewer trades and raising variance; trading every signal at a fixed per-trade risk spreads the book across many small trades.
setup_summary: With a fixed per-trade risk limit (e.g., 1% = $50 on a $5,000 account), choose contract granularity (micro vs mini lot) so that every generated signal is tradable; trade all signals to spread PnL and reduce per-trade concentration; scale up only as capital and retained profits grow.
trigger_invalidation: Trade-every-signal presumes signal breadth is beneficial; invalid if the signal set is unfiltered/low-quality or if it would breach portfolio constraints — in V8 terms, one-exposure-per-(instrument, direction) and the heat cap override it.
risk_geometry: Fixed per-trade risk (author's 1% default; 0.25% during the training phase); granularity chosen so the worst-case loss fits the account; no entry/stop/target specifics.

strategy_name: RSI BAMM divergence reversal with harmonic pattern confluence
setup_summary: On the 1h bar: (1) RSI first tests an extreme limit (overbought >70 / oversold <30); (2) an M-type (bearish) or W-type (bullish) complex RSI structure completes; (3) RSI retests the 50 limit at minimum; (4) a Trigger Bar is defined - if the Trigger Bar is the extreme price high/low the Confirmation Point completes at the 1.618 extension (usually Crab/Deep Crab), otherwise at 1.13 (Bat/Butterfly/5-0/Gartley); (5) RSI diverges from price as price makes a new extreme while the impulsive RSI retest does NOT exceed the prior complex-structure extreme; (6) entry when price simultaneously completes the harmonic pattern at its PRZ at the RSI BAMM Confirmation Point.
trigger_invalidation: Thesis invalid if the impulsive RSI retest exceeds the reading of the prior complex structure (no divergence), or if price violates the extension stop zone - beyond 1.618 for a 1.13 setup, beyond 2.0 for a 1.618 setup - especially on the first test, which instead flags strong primary-trend continuation.
risk_geometry: Entry at bar close after the harmonic pattern completes at the PRZ/Confirmation Point; stop beyond the defining extension (1.618 for 1.13 setups; 2.0 for 1.618 setups); reversal expected to be quick after the zone test ('most valid reversals will occur quickly after this area has been tested'); no expiry specified beyond the acceleration window of a few bars.
quote: The execution of the trade is triggered at the completion of the relative harmonic pattern that completes at the appropriate RSI BAMM extension level.

strategy_name: RSI BAMM Reversal Acceleration Trigger (M-type indicator breakdown)

strategy_name: Slingshot - failed-high reversal with measured target and scale-out ladder
mechanism: a failed higher high after a clear key-high/key-low structure shows the bull leg is over; breaking the key low confirms the reversal, and the key-high-to-key-low range projects a measured target with high odds
setup_summary: Identify Key High (any high above the prior high), then Key Low (a 2-3 bar swing low), then Slingshot High (a failed high at least 3 bars from a prior higher bar that is within 20 days - both confirmations required so you are not buying a running top or picking a bottom). Sell on a break of the Key Low with ADX rising; stop = Slingshot High, set as a reversal stop (failed signal is a signal). Profit objective = Key Low minus (Slingshot High minus Key Low); take half off at 1x target, further halves at 2x/3x, trailing stop at 50% of a profit target; final unit exits on stop or Bishop. Mini-slingshot drops the 20-day confirmation, takes 100% off at target, and moves stop to breakeven at the half-way point.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: break of the Key Low after a confirmed Slingshot High. Invalidated when the Slingshot High stop (reversal) is hit or the measured target ladder completes; divergence from the measured projection is not itself an exit.
risk_geometry: Entry: sell stop on Key Low break. Stop: Slingshot High (reversal stop, i.e., exit-and-flip). Target: measured projection (Key Low - [Slingshot High - Key Low]); scale-outs at 1x/2x/3x target with a 50%-of-target trailing stop; final unit on stop or Bishop. Requires at least 2 contracts.
quote: The first profit objective is calculated this way. Take the difference between the slingshot high and the key low. Now subtract that value from the key low.

strategy_name: RSI BAMM divergence confirmation (complex RSI structure + harmonic PRZ)
mechanism: A complex (W/M-type) RSI structure built entirely beyond the extreme line creates measurable divergence: on the final retest the price makes a nominal new extreme while the RSI holds above/below its prior reading, then the reversal completes at a 1.13 or 1.618 extension of the initial reaction.
setup_summary: With RSI(14): (1) RSI forms a complex W-type entirely below 30 (bullish) or M-type entirely above 70 (bearish); (2) the Trigger Bar is the price bar that closes RSI back above 30 / below 70, and its extreme marks the minimum retest level; (3) RSI must retrace to at least the 50 mid-line; (4) final divergence: price makes a nominal new low/high while RSI at an impulsive retest holds above/below its prior reading; (5) Confirmation Point completes at 1.13 extension (Trigger Bar 2-4 bars from the extreme) or 1.618 extension (Trigger Bar IS the extreme), ideally converging with a harmonic pattern (Bat/Gartley/Butterfly/Crab/5-0) completion.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: complex structure + Trigger Bar + RSI mid-50 retrace + impulsive retest holding the prior RSI reading + price nominal new extreme. Invalid: RSI never tests 50, RSI violates its prior reading on the retest (non-impulsive), price exceeds the prior extreme materially, or extensions are exceeded (beyond 2.0).
risk_geometry: Entry: bar close at the Confirmation Point coordinating with the harmonic PRZ; stop: beyond 1.618 for 1.13 setups, beyond 2.0 for 1.618 setups (do-or-die); optional Acceleration Trigger (W-type above 30 after confirmation) as an entry filter; reversal expected quickly after the nominal new extreme.

strategy_name: RSI BAMM extension stop and do-or-die invalidation
mechanism: Setup validity is defined by a hard invalidation beyond the confirmation extension: for 1.13-confirmation setups the stop zone is beyond 1.618; for 1.618 setups beyond 2.0; tandem violation of both the RSI BAMM extension and the pattern PRZ = failed setup.
setup_summary: For any RSI BAMM trade, the stop/invalidation is a deterministic function of the confirmation extension: valid reversals do not exceed the confirmation extension by much; 1.13 setups are invalidated beyond the 1.618 of the final move, 1.618 setups beyond the 2.0. Violations, especially on the first test, flag a strong primary trend.
trigger_invalidation: Stop: beyond 1.618 for 1.13-confirmation setups; beyond 2.0 for 1.618-confirmation setups. Failure: tandem violation of the extension and the pattern PRZ; early warning = PRZ violation in the upper/lower range before the extension is even reached.
risk_geometry: Stop: beyond the next harmonic extension of the final move (1.618 or 2.0). No target changes — exit at reversal continuation; do-or-die discipline with little discretion.
quote: As a general rule, the 1.13 extension typically employs the area beyond the 1.618 to define its stop loss zone. In comparison, those situations that trigger a 1.618 extension will typically define the area beyond the 2.0 as a violation of the setup.
