notes: Concrete, deterministic stop logic usable in RiskGate admission and lifecycle dead-thesis checks. Complements the atr_stop/stop_distance_atr vocabulary with ratio-based invalidation; first-test-violation-flag also functions as a trend-strength signal.
book: Harmonic Trading, Volume Two - Advanced Strategies for Profiting from the Natural Order of the Financial Markets 2010

strategy_name: Multi-Oscillator Extreme Confluence Reversal (leg-in trigger)
mechanism: Short-term overextension: when at least two independent oscillators (RSI(5), Stoch %K(5), CCI(20)) simultaneously register oversold/overbought, price tends to move opposite within ~3 days - used here as the pre-event 'leg in' timing device.
setup_summary: On a daily chart, oversold if RSI(5)<30, Stoch %K(5)<25, CCI(20)<-100; overbought if >70, >75, >+100. Requiring agreement from any two registers the extreme condition; then expect the opposite-direction move within roughly three sessions (buy calls if oversold, puts if overbought).
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: 2-of-3 oscillators at extreme. Invalidation: trend continuing to new extremes (no bounce); the book uses it as a 3-day timing signal, not a hold.
risk_geometry: Entry: at the close of the signal day. Stop/target: not stated for the reversal itself (it is a timing filter for the straddle leg-in).
quote: We need agreement from any two of these indicators to register an oversold or overbought condition. If we get such a condition, then we will leg into the trade.
chapter_anchor: Ch. 13 'Options Strategies: Neutral' - The Straddle Strategy: An 11-Point Review (p. 306; file lines 242-261)
notes: Fully computable on crypto OHLCV; the 2-of-3 confluence is a cheap falsifiable variant of rsi_oversold_reversal. Caveat for 24/7 no-gap markets: oscillator extremes form intraday differently than on exchange-gapped daily bars; the 3-day bounce horizon is testable as a BACKLOG candidate.
book: Trend Trading for a Living - Learn the Skills and Gain the Confidence to Trade for a Living 2007

strategy_name: Historical Event-Move Size as Selection Feature
mechanism: Prior event-move magnitude is persistent for an instrument: selecting only stocks that gapped >$1.00 at their last two earnings, and preferring higher-priced, more volatile, high-beta names, concentrates the universe on instruments that actually deliver event moves.
setup_summary: Filter the event-play universe: require >1M shares/day, beta >=2.0, price >=$40, and a gap >$1.00 at each of the last two scheduled announcements; 'the larger the dollar amount of the gap, however, the more proﬁtable the trade will be.'
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: history of large event gaps + liquidity + beta + price filters. Invalidation: 'quiet market cycles when even the most volatile of stocks do not move that much in response to earnings.'
risk_geometry: Selection filter only - no entry/stop/target.
quote: This is why it is so important to select stocks that are higher in price, are very volatile, and have had a history of multibucker gaps at earnings.
chapter_anchor: Ch. 13 'Options Strategies: Neutral' - Taking Off a Straddle (p. 304; file lines 170-174)
notes: Clean, falsifiable feature input: for crypto macro events, average |price move| around prior FOMC/CPI releases (and prior listing/listing-futures events) as a per-instrument selection feature. Event calendar for crypto is sparser than equity earnings season, hence MEDIUM.
book: Trend Trading for a Living - Learn the Skills and Gain the Confidence to Trade for a Living 2007

strategy_name: Range-cycle compression/expansion regime (small ranges beget large ranges) with open-to-close direction law
mechanism: Range sizes oscillate in clusters: compression of ranges precedes expansion; on large-range days, close position vs open carries directional information (up days open near low and close near high)
setup_summary: Falsifiable timing/regime rule: after a series of small-range bars (relative to a trailing average) a large-range bar becomes likely — wait for ranges to 'dry up' before entering volatility-breakout trades, and expect contraction after large-range days. Directional law (T-Bond study 1970-98): ~87% of closes are above the open when the open-to-low dip is <20% of the day's range; a positive open-to-close of $500+ occurs 42% of the time and $1,000+ 15% of the time if the dip is <10%; there is near-zero chance of a large up close after a 70-80% dip below the open.
trigger_invalidation: Expansion fails to arrive within the expected window (compression persists); or a would-be large-range day dips far below the open (dip >70-80% of range), making a positive open-to-close near-impossible
risk_geometry: Not a standalone entry — a timing/direction filter over other setups; when applied directly: enter at open, exit at close, stop = reference range fraction
quote: Small ranges beget large ranges. Large ranges beget small ranges.
chapter_anchor: Chapter 2, 'The Natural Cycle of Range Change' and 'The Importance of the Open to Low or High of the Day' (pp. 27-36)
notes: Directly usable as a volatility feature (range percentile vs trailing window) plus a regime gate for the volatility_breakout family. Open-to-close statistics map onto per-bar response features in the 1h timeframe.
book: Long-Term Secrets to Short-Term Trading 1999

strategy_name: Hold-to-close / time-as-profit exit methodology
mechanism: Profit grows with holding time; exits before the period close truncate the large-range days that pay for small-range losses; fixed intraday profit targets systematically underperform holding to the close
setup_summary: Comparative, falsifiable: S&P system buying the Monday open after a Friday down close — with a $500 fixed target it lost $8,150; with a $1,000 target it made $13,737; with exit-at-close it made $39,075 ($100/trade avg, smaller drawdown); holding 6 days made $71,600. Rule: never take a winner off before the close of the trading period; use the 'bailout' (exit on the first profitable opening) for fast markets and delay it 1-2 days for slower ones; always keep a dollar stop; exit-and-reverse on an opposite signal.
trigger_invalidation: n/a (methodology; applies to exit selection given any entry)
risk_geometry: exit = period close, or first profitable opening (bailout), or N bars after entry; dollar stop always in force beneath any exit rule
quote: The most profitable short-term trading strategy I know and use is to enter the trade, place my protective stop, then shut my eyes... and wait to get out on the close.
chapter_anchor: Chapter 3, 'The Real Secret to Short-Term Trading' (pp. 45-55); exit rules in Chapter 11 (p. 157)
notes: Supports V8's fill-at-close simulator and the principle that expiry_bars / close exits should not be replaced by tight profit targets. In 24/7 perps the 'close' maps to the trading-period boundary.
book: Long-Term Secrets to Short-Term Trading 1999

strategy_name: Oops! gap-overreaction reversal (open beyond prior extreme, reclaimed)
mechanism: An open far beyond the prior period's range is an emotional overreaction (stops run, panic flow); if price then reclaims the prior period's extreme, the overreaction reverses sharply with trapped flow as fuel
setup_summary: Falsifiable: LONG — a bar opens BELOW the prior bar's low (a rare occurrence; price almost always opens within the prior range); enter long when price rallies back to the prior bar's low. SHORT — a bar opens ABOVE the prior bar's high; enter short when price falls back to the prior bar's high. Exit next day's open (trade usually lasts ~1.5 days), flat dollar stop. Williams reports S&P 82%+ accuracy (best days except Wed/Thu, $438/trade avg, $42,687) and bonds 86% accuracy ($201/trade); selling into a 9-day overbought filter on Wednesdays netted 79-89% accuracy.
trigger_invalidation: No reclaim of the prior extreme within 1-2 bars, or the gap extreme is exceeded again (gap continuation instead of reversal)
risk_geometry: entry: stop/limit at the prior extreme after the gap open; stop: flat dollar (S&P $2,000 / bonds $1,800); target: next period open (bailout); expiry: 1-2 bars
quote: The precise overreaction we are looking for to give us a buy signal is an opening that is below the previous day's low... The entry comes when, following the lower open, price then rallies back to the previous day's low.
chapter_anchor: Chapter 7, 'Oops! This Is Not a Mistake' (pp. 113-120)
notes: True daily-boundary gaps do not exist in 24/7 perps, but the pattern maps to period-boundary overextension wicks beyond prior extremes on any timeframe, and to liquidation-cascade stop runs. Conceptual cousin of v8's liquidity_sweep_reclaim family (sweep of a prior extreme + reclaim), but the trigger is an open-gap, not a close-position sweep. Registry candidate under the complexity budget.
book: Long-Term Secrets to Short-Term Trading 1999

strategy_name: Trade-day-of-week (TDW) and trading-day-of-month (TDM) calendar biases
mechanism: Specific weekdays and trading days of the month carry persistent directional/volatility biases (S&P up Mondays, bonds up Tuesdays, grains up Wednesdays, first-of-month and end-of-month rallies), contradicting a memoryless random walk
setup_summary: Falsifiable statistical claims over 17-30 years of data: S&P 500 closes above the Monday open 57% of the time (avg +$109/trade); bonds are best on Tuesdays; grains rally most on Wednesdays (1968-98); both stocks and bonds rally around the first of the month (S&P first-trade-day-of-month buy: 85% accuracy on 129 trades, $73,437); bonds rally into month-end (TDM 18/22 buy, up to 89% accuracy with a gold-downtrend filter) and dip mid-month (TDM 12 sell, 76% accuracy). TDM counts trading days, not calendar days. Williams uses these as stacked filters over other setups, never standalone.
trigger_invalidation: Bias window passes without the expected move; or the stacked filter (e.g., bond trend, gold trend) fails
risk_geometry: entry: open of the bias day (+ X% of prior range as an expansion filter); stop: flat dollar ($1,100-2,500, often only after entry day); target: close, first profitable opening, or exit 3 days after entry
quote: stocks have a proven proclivity to rally on Mondays, Bonds on Tuesdays and virtually all the grains on Wednesday.
chapter_anchor: Chapter 6, 'The Market Is Not a Coin Flip' (pp. 82-88); Chapter 10, 'Special Short-Term Situations' (pp. 147-156)
notes: Calendar features (weekday, trading-day-of-month, month-end proximity) are deterministic from event timestamps, so they do not violate the no-wall-clock rule. In 24/7 perps the daily open/close framing weakens, but day-of-week volume/vol regimes and CME futures/option expiry (end-of-month/quarter) effects persist.
book: Long-Term Secrets to Short-Term Trading 1999

strategy_name: Volume Climax Reversal (Buying/Selling Climax + Stopping Volume)
mechanism: climax_exhaustion
setup_summary: In a mature trend, a wide-range bar prints on ultra-high volume but fails to follow through (next candles are narrow spread, or a deep-wick hammer forms), showing absorption at the extreme. Confirmation comes as a low-volume test (small hammer on low volume) after the high-volume absorption; enter on next-bar close on the reclaimed side. Sell side analog: narrow-spread up candle on very high volume at a cycle top (buying climax) followed by weak candles.
trigger_invalidation: Trend-extreme bar prints on normal (not ultra-high) volume; a low-volume test is followed by a fresh high-volume continuation through the extreme; no stopping volume (rising volume + narrowing spread) appears, so any reversal is not durable.
risk_geometry: Entry on bar close on the reclaimed side; stop beyond the climax extreme (wick/high or low); target opposite side of the congestion level; expiry multi-bar.
quote: if this pair were going to sell off sharply, then we would expect this to be a wide spread down candle – it isn't. It's a narrow spread.
chapter_anchor: Ch 10, Fig 10.17 Selling Climax and Fig 10.18 Buying Climax (AUD/USD weekly)
notes: Corroborates V8 backlog family capitulation (capitulation_exhaustion) with explicit stopping-volume/absorption criteria plus a low-volume-test confirmation step. 24/7 crypto perps with high leverage produce frequent climactic volume extremes and liquidation cascades, so the pattern is testable on BTCUSDT 1h. Caveat: aggregated perp volume mixes venues; use a consistent volume source.
book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis 2013

strategy_name: Triple Top / Triple Bottom Level Reversal
mechanism: level_rejection
setup_summary: Price tests a well-defined resistance level three times, failing each time (triple top), or tests support three times and bounces (triple bottom). Enter on the third-touch failure confirmed by VPA (reversal candle on above-average volume); alternatively, a break-and-hold beyond the level builds a strong platform of support/resistance for a continuation trade.
trigger_invalidation: Price breaks cleanly through the level on strong volume (reversal of the reversal thesis); the third touch succeeds in pushing through on volume.
risk_geometry: Entry bar close on third-touch failure; stop beyond the tested level; target opposite congestion or measured move.
quote: the pair has tested the 1.0600 level on three separate occasions... failing on each occasion.
chapter_anchor: Ch 11, Fig 11.16 (AUD/USD daily triple top) and Fig 11.17 (EUR/CHF hourly triple bottom)
notes: Multi-touch levels are common in crypto because of clustered limit orders and liquidation walls, but 24/7 price discovery makes levels less sticky than in gapped markets. Volume confirmation at the touch is the falsifiable gate. Candidate variant of the supply_demand_zone family.
book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis 2013

strategy_name: Effort-vs-result volume/price anomaly detector
mechanism: Wyckoff's law of effort vs result: wide-range price requires proportionally high volume; when spread and volume disagree (wide spread + low volume, or narrow spread + high volume) the price action is suspect - marked, not genuine.
setup_summary: Single-bar or multi-bar detector: a wide-spread candle on LOW volume is an anomaly (likely a trap/engineered move - insiders testing or marking price, not joining); a narrow-spread candle on HIGH volume is an anomaly (absorption - longs liquidating at a top, buyers absorbing at a bottom; effort without result = market struggling at this level). A valid trend shows rising price with rising volume, and falling price with rising volume; a rising market with falling volume is a classic sign of weakness.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: divergence between spread and volume on a bar or small group of bars. Invalidation: volume normalizes to validate subsequent bars (divergence was a one-off), or divergence appears without trend context (book: get bearings first - location in trend is the first reference point).
risk_geometry: Book-level tool: used to exit existing positions, stand aside, or prepare a reversal entry; no stop/target; it is a confirmation/flagging primitive feeding other setups.
quote: The small price increase has been generated by a huge amount of volume, so clearly something is wrong.
chapter_anchor: Ch.4 - Examples Of Anomalies; Ch.6 - Wide/Narrow Spread Candles
notes: Propose as a marketstate feature (spread/volume agreement score) consumed by expert still_valid logic and RiskGate: e.g., trend_pullback longs should not be added while effort-result divergence signals engineered price.
book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis 2013

strategy_name: Multi-swing reversal structures (double top/bottom, triple top, head-and-shoulders) confirmed by a close through the pattern
mechanism: Repeated tests of a level accumulate supply/demand; a decisive close through the confirmation line completes the reversal, filtering consolidation that would otherwise resemble the pattern
setup_summary: Double bottom: two prominent near-parallel bottoms in a downtrend, valid on a close above the middle of the 'W'. Double top: mirror, valid on a close below the middle of the 'M'. Head-and-shoulders top (three-Buddha): valid on a close below the neckline connecting the swing lows on both sides of the head. Triple top: valid on a close below the lowest point between the three peaks. The book stresses that many double/triple tops resolve as consolidation, so the close-through confirmation is the validity filter (SUN bonus: peaks 4/7/9 formed a triple top / head-and-shoulders warning).
trigger_invalidation: Pattern is invalid without the close-through confirmation; many such patterns turn out to be consolidation periods, so the confirmation line is the falsification point.
risk_geometry: Entry on the confirming close through the line; stop back inside the pattern (above the middle); target = pattern projection / prior swing.
quote: It is a valid reversal pattern when it is confirmed by a close below the middle of the 'M'... Remember that many double and triple top patterns turn out to be periods of consolidation.
chapter_anchor: Glossary (Double bottom, Double top, Head-and-shoulders top, Triple top); Ch. 11 Case Study 1 bonus (SUN triple top at peaks 4/7/9)
notes: Swing detection plus close-through confirmation is implementable on 1h BTC, but base rates of these patterns are contested and require a structural (swing/pattern) feature pipeline; the close-through confirmation is the falsifiable core.
book: Getting Started in Candlestick Charting 2008

strategy_name: Stochastic oscillator oversold/overbought confirmation at support/resistance for reversal candles
mechanism: An oscillator at an extreme while a reversal candle forms at S/R confirms that the counter-move has a catalyst rather than just a wick
setup_summary: The stochastic oscillator (12-3-3 in the book's chart panels) in oversold territory confirms bullish reversal candles at support (long), and overbought confirms bearish reversal candles at resistance (short). Used consistently across all three case studies: SUN #1 oversold dragonfly doji at the 50-SMA; SUN #7/#4 overbought stochastic with bearish reversal candles; MEOH #7 overbought dark cloud cover; WOLF #1 oversold hammer at the 200-SMA.
trigger_invalidation: In strong trends the stochastic can remain pinned at extremes; oscillator confirmation is only treated as valid at S/R context, and by itself it is a confirmation feature, not an entry.
risk_geometry: Entry at the confirmed reversal close; stop beyond S/R; target = opposite S/R.
quote: The stochastic oscillator had reached the oversold line as well offering further confirmation of a viable setup for a long position.
chapter_anchor: Ch. 11 Case Study 1 (SUN #1); Case Study 2 (MEOH #7); Case Study 3 (WOLF #1)
notes: Computable on any bar series; in V8 this is a 'response' feature-group input that gates the candlestick-reversal families, complementary to the overextension feature (distance from mean) rather than a duplicate.
book: Getting Started in Candlestick Charting 2008

strategy_name: Oscillator overbought/oversold confluence for candlestick reversal signals
mechanism: When price is overextended (stochastic >80 or <20, and/or far from the MA), a candlestick reversal signal has more fuel because the move is already vulnerable to profit-taking and reversion to the mean.
setup_summary: Score candlestick reversal signals with overextension features: stochastic (14-5-5) in overbought (>80) territory when a bearish pattern forms, or oversold (<20) when a bullish pattern forms; and/or price far from the 20-SMA. The book's rule: either condition alone raises the odds, and requiring both is NOT recommended because they often co-occur but not always — the feature should be additive, not gating.
trigger_invalidation: In strong trends overbought/oversold persists (book: 'it takes a consensus by many market participants to reverse a strong trend'), so these readings are short-term warnings, not trend-reversal signals; the book shows a counterexample where the oscillator gave no confirmation yet the setup still followed through.
risk_geometry: Filter/feature only; it strengthens entries already defined by the candlestick pattern and sets no stop/target of its own.
quote: If a bearish candlestick reversal pattern forms while stochastic is in overbought territory, or if a bullish reversal pattern forms while stochastic is in oversold territory, it strengthens the candlestick signal.
chapter_anchor: Ch 7, Overbought and Oversold Conditions / Enhanced Candlestick Signals, pp.146-149
notes: This is a response-group feature (momentum/oscillator extremes) added to the MarketState for reversal-pattern families, not a standalone expert. In strong crypto trends, overbought persistence is common — consistent with the book's short-term-only interpretation.
book: Getting Started in Candlestick Charting 2008

strategy_name: Confidence-band (dispersion-first) positioning
setup_summary: Design positions from the width of the uncertainty band around a forecast, not the point forecast: in high-dispersion regimes (wide error band) reduce size, widen stops and extend expiry; in low-dispersion regimes the same point forecast justifies tighter risk. The actionable quantity is variance around the estimate, not the estimate itself.
trigger_invalidation: Rule adds no value if dispersion-scaled sizing produces no risk-adjusted improvement versus constant sizing on frozen OOS.
risk_geometry: Stop distance and size scale with the error band (dispersion), never with the point forecast alone; no fixed R target stated.
quote: my activity in the market depends far less on where I think the market is going so much as it does on the degree of error I allow around such a confidence level
chapter_anchor: Ch. 11 'We Do Not Understand Confidence Levels' (p. 168)
notes: Aligns with ATR-based risk_geometry but adds the normative point: heat/stop/expiry are outputs of dispersion, not of conviction. Reached as DESIGN_INFERENCE; V8 already ATR-scales, so marginal contribution is the sizing-as-output-of-variance discipline.
book: Fooled by Randomness - The Hidden Role of Chance in Life and in the Markets 2005

strategy_name: Valuation overshoot reversion (Shiller)
mechanism: Prices overreact to fundamentals, running too high on good news and too low on bad, then revert toward the fundamental proxy
setup_summary: Shiller's 1981 finding (cited in the book): if a price is the estimated value of discounted cash flows, then market prices are far too volatile relative to the fundamentals they reflect — visibly overshooting in both directions, which contradicts rational-expectation efficiency. Tradeable family for crypto perps: build a value proxy (funding/basis, realized-vol-based fair range, or carry) and fade price when it deviates by a large multiple of the proxy, expecting reversion.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: extreme price-vs-proxy deviation. Invalid: proxy keeps expanding (funding/basis stays extreme) with no reversion within the expiry horizon; regime change breaks the proxy.
risk_geometry: Entry: bar close or limit at the extreme; stop: beyond the valuation proxy by a multiple; target: reversion to proxy mean; expiry: bounded (weeks-to-months scale per the book's 'market is too volatile relative to fundamentals' claim).
quote: Prices swing more than the fundamentals they are supposed to reflect, they visibly overreact by being too high at times (when their price overshoots the good news or when they go up without any marked reason) or too low at others.
chapter_anchor: Ch. 3, Shiller Redux (p. 53-54)
notes: The book states the inefficiency and overreaction but not a tradable setup, so this is a backlog family candidate gated on a defensible perp value proxy (no clean dividends/cash flows for BTC). The book also notes the peso-problem corollary: 'currencies that exhibit the largest historical stability are the most prone to crashes' — calm-waters regimes precede violent breaks, relevant to volatility-compression fade setups.
book: Fooled by Randomness - The Hidden Role of Chance in Life and in the Markets 2005

strategy_name: Z-score / Bollinger band mean reversion on a stationary series (entry/exit z-score levels)
mechanism: an OU-style pull toward a moving mean is exploitable only within a band; enter on deviation, exit on reversion to the mean
setup_summary: On a stationary or cointegrated price/spread series with a short half-life, enter long when z-score = (price - movingAvg)/(movingStd) crosses below -entryZscore, exit when it reverts to -exitZscore (e.g., 0); short is the mirror. One unit at a time (all-in). Author backtest on the GLD-USO spread: APR 17.8%, Sharpe 0.96 (no transaction costs; prototype). Lookback can be set to the half-life instead of optimized.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: z-score beyond entryZscore band on a series that passed stationarity/half-life gating. Invalidation: the series stops reverting - z-score fails to reach exitZscore within a horizon, or half-life lengthens / cointegration breaks (as GLD-GDX did after the July 2008 oil spike).
risk_geometry: Entry NEXT_BAR_CLOSE on the spread/portfolio; target = exitZscore (0 = current mean); stop = none by design (stops contradict mean reversion, see risk-rule finding); expiry = small multiple of half-life lookback.
quote: we can enter into a position only when the price deviates by more than entryZscore standard deviations from the mean... We can exit when the price mean-reverts to exitZscore standard deviations from the mean
chapter_anchor: Chapter 3, 'Bollinger Bands' / Example 3.2 (see also Chapter 2 linear strategy)
notes: Directly testable on BTCUSDT 1h price or on a funding/basis spread series; requires the stationarity/half-life gate (next finding) before admission. entryZscore/exitZscore/lookback become family variants, one multiplicity unit.
book: Algorithmic Trading - Winning Strategies and Their Rationale 2013

strategy_name: Stationarity and half-life gating before any mean-reversion trading
mechanism: only series whose next move depends on current level (ADF lambda<0) or whose variance diffuses sublinearly (Hurst<0.5, VR test) can profit from mean reversion; half-life sets the natural time scale
setup_summary: Before trading a series mean-reverting, run the ADF test (lambda/SE, 90%+ level), Hurst exponent (H<0.5), and Variance Ratio test; then regress deltaY on lag(Y) to get lambda and half-life = -log(2)/lambda. Only trade series that are stationary (or cointegrating, via CADF or Johansen eigenvector) with half-life short enough for the trading horizon. Set lookback and holding period to a small multiple of the half-life instead of brute-force optimization. A positive or near-zero lambda means do not trade it mean-reverting.
trigger_invalidation: Half-life too long for the horizon, or lambda positive, rejects the mean-reversion model for that series; revalidate when the cointegration relationship breaks (e.g., GLD-GDX).
risk_geometry: No trade geometry; it is a parameter-selection method (lookback = c x half-life).
quote: this lambda also determines a natural time scale for many parameters in our strategy... Often, setting the look-back to equal a small multiple of the half-life is close to optimal
chapter_anchor: Chapter 2, 'Half-Life of Mean Reversion' (ADF, Hurst/Variance Ratio, CADF, Johansen)
notes: V8 gating rule: a mean-reversion family Expert should only be admitted when a point-in-time stationarity/half-life gate passes on the traded series or spread; this is a methodology/lifecycle input, not a strategy. Important because most price series (incl. BTC) are geometric random walks and will fail the gate.
book: Algorithmic Trading - Winning Strategies and Their Rationale 2013

strategy_name: Mean reversion of volatility and volatility-index anti-correlation (VX-ES stationary portfolio)
mechanism: volatility is stationary and anti-correlated with the underlying index, so a constant-hedge-ratio long-vol/long-index portfolio is stationary and band-tradeable
setup_summary: The VIX index is stationary by ADF at 99%, but VX front futures are in persistent contango (average annualized roll return about -50%) so VX price itself does not mean-revert; the VX back/front ratio does (ADF stationary at 99%, linear MR APR 17.7%, Sharpe 1.5). Volatility is strongly anti-correlated with the equity index (VX-ES daily-return correlation about -75%): a stationary portfolio long 0.3906 VX + long 1 ES (prices scaled by contract multipliers), traded with a Bollinger band on the regression residuals, gives APR 12.3%, Sharpe 1.4 on the test set.
trigger_invalidation: Volatility regime change (author documents two regimes 2004-2008 vs 2008-2012: lower level, wider range); correlation breaks; mixing regimes invalidates the regression/hedge ratio.
risk_geometry: Bollinger entry at +-1 std of stationary-portfolio residuals; hedge ratio fixed from a 500-day training set, then traded out-of-sample.
quote: volatility is anti-correlated with the stock equity market index: When the market goes down, volatility shoots up, and to a lesser extent, vice versa
chapter_anchor: Chapter 5, 'Volatility Futures versus Equity Index Futures' (Figure 5.10-5.12)
notes: V8 has no vol instrument; implement as a realized-volatility feature (from OHLC) and a vol-mean-reversion regime/filter gate rather than a traded expert. The regime-split warning (do not regress across regimes) is directly applicable to V8 gating.
book: Algorithmic Trading - Winning Strategies and Their Rationale 2013

strategy_name: Data errors inflate mean-reversion backtests and poison spread strategies; deflate momentum backtests
mechanism: a single erroneous outlier price creates a fictitious entry at the bad level and a mean-reverting-looking return when price returns to truth; errors are large relative to small spreads
setup_summary: An outlier (e.g., a bogus $110 print on a $100 stock) produces fictitious mean-reversion profit (short at 110, cover at 100) and fictitious momentum loss (buy at 110, stopped at 100) in backtests, and real losing trades in live execution when erroneous bid/ask quotes trigger orders. Spread and arbitrage strategies are most sensitive because the error is a large fraction of the small spread (a $1 error on a $5 spread is 20%). Currency venues especially: no regulation requires trade-price reporting; bid-ask spread varies by venue, so costs are venue-dependent.
trigger_invalidation: N/A - data-quality gate for the V8 lab/data pipeline.
risk_geometry: No trade geometry; data-cleaning requirement (exchange cancel-and-correct codes, primary-exchange prices, synchronized settlement prices for spreads).
quote: If there are errors, or 'outliers,' in the historical data used for backtesting, then these errors usually inflate the backtest performance of mean-reverting strategies.
chapter_anchor: Chapter 3, 'The Danger of Data Errors' (see also Chapter 1 pitfalls: look-ahead, survivorship, primary vs consolidated, futures roll/settlement)
notes: V8 lab/source-integrity rule: mean-reversion backtests are a canary for tape errors; re-run any z-score/band expert result with spike-filtered data. The pitfall taxonomy in Chapter 1 (look-ahead, survivorship, primary-vs-consolidated, futures close-vs-settlement, roll back-adjustment) is a checklist for the V8 data pipeline.

strategy_name: Venue/custody counterparty risk (MF Global failure)
setup_summary: MF Global's October 2011 bankruptcy froze cash (a wire never landed) and orphaned positions between two brokers; the author was able to transfer most positions beforehand and keeps accounts at multiple brokers. Falsifiable operational rule: no single venue may hold both all cash and all positions; venue failure must not prevent exit or admission.
trigger_invalidation: None -- operational risk rule.
risk_geometry: No geometry; portfolio/operations-level rule: split venues, keep executable positions transferable.
quote: I was all in cash, and my cash was supposed to have been wired on the Friday before the collapse. This did not happen and my cash at MF Global was frozen.
chapter_anchor: Ch.10 Trade Journal, pp.191-192
notes: The exact analog for crypto perp venue risk (Mt. Gox, FTX). For V8 this lands as a RiskGate/operational rule once execution exists; in the PRE-EXPERIMENTAL phase it is a standing risk rule for the program's venue/custody assumptions. The simulator's assumption that fills occur at the venue is unaffected but the program must not assume venue solvency.
book: The Trend Following Bible - How Professional Traders Compound Wealth and Manage Risk 2012

strategy_name: Preplanned systematic profit-taking
mechanism: a profit exit decided in advance prevents a winning trade from silently reversing into a loser
setup_summary: For every entry the trader fixes in advance the price/point at which profits will be taken, so a winner can never turn into a loser and 'leaving money on the table' is a managed variable. Claim: not having an organized, systematic money-management regimen for taking profits is one of the three most common and costliest trading errors.
trigger_invalidation: Violated when an open winning position is held with no pre-set target or the target is moved to chase the move.
risk_geometry: Target: fixed price/R-multiple known in advance ('in most cases I know for sure at what point I am going to take my profits'); this is V8's target_r.
quote: Why would you ever let a winning trade turn into a loser, or not have a systematic way of taking profits, if you weren't convinced the market was going your way indefinitely?
chapter_anchor: Ch 7, 'Eliminating the Emotional Risk'
notes: Encodes as target_r in V8 risk_geometry; profit exit must be rule-based (pre-set level), not discretionary, which is exactly the frozen-ref style of the existing experts.
book: Trading in the Zone - Master the Market with Confidence, Discipline and a Winning Attitude 2000

strategy_name: Outcome recency bias: sizing and risk perception invariant to the last few trades
mechanism: the last 2-3 outcomes distort perceived risk — overconfidence after wins drives oversizing and rule violation (euphoria), fear after losses drives hesitation — producing boom-bust equity
setup_summary: A typical trader's perceived risk in any situation is a function of the outcome of his most recent two or three trades: after a win streak he sizes up ('loading up'), stops perceiving risk, and violates rules; after losses he hesitates and skips valid signals. Claim: consistent winners' risk perception and position size are unaffected by recent outcomes; boom-bust cycles end in huge losses caused by euphoria or self-sabotage after winning streaks.
trigger_invalidation: Violated when position size or risk tolerance varies with recent P&L; the guard is fixed sizing independent of the outcome sequence.
risk_geometry: Position size fixed by pre-defined risk per trade, not by confidence; heat cap and one-exposure-per-(instrument,direction) make euphoria-driven sizing structurally impossible.
quote: It's when you're winning that you are most susceptible to making a mistake, overtrading, putting on too large a position, violating your rules
chapter_anchor: Ch 3, 'Winners, Losers, Boomers, and Busters'; Ch 6 opening
notes: Human emotion is absent in V8 automation, but the same failure can enter through sizing rules conditioned on rolling performance or promotion decisions made after hot streaks; the guard is outcome-invariant risk sizing. The book's 'every loss puts you that much closer to a win' is a psychological reframe that contradicts its own statistical-independence claim — do not encode it as a regime filter or edge modifier.
book: Trading in the Zone - Master the Market with Confidence, Discipline and a Winning Attitude 2000

strategy_name: Volatility-led risk-on/risk-off regime filter
mechanism: Volatility spikes precede risk aversion; capital rotates out of risk assets into safe havens, so volatility regime leads directional bias across risk-sensitive assets
setup_summary: When realized (or implied) volatility spikes, treat the regime as risk-off: reduce long-risk exposure and expect flight-to-quality; 'rising/spiking (falling) volatility in the forex markets often precedes an appreciation (depreciation) in the Japanese yen.' Book documents risk-on/risk-off rotations (2008 credit crisis flight to yen/franc/dollar; 2010-11 EUR/USD trading as a risk proxy with S&P 500 moves often preceding, not mirroring, EUR/USD).
trigger_invalidation: Regime feature: RISK_OFF when volatility crosses up a threshold; invalidates when vol mean-reverts without regime change (false alarm - 2011 example: post-earthquake vol spike was followed by intervention, not a persistent risk-off).
risk_geometry: Filter/gate only - modulates exposure and which families are admissible, not an entry geometry.
quote: rising/spiking (falling) volatility in the forex markets often precedes an appreciation (depreciation) in the Japanese yen.
chapter_anchor: Ch.3 'Risk-Driven Trading' pp.84-85; Ch.5 'Sentiment Analysis' pp.115-119
notes: For BTCUSDT there is no intra-market safe haven, but the vol-spike-to-risk-off mapping is usable as a regime gate (equity vol / crypto vol spike precedes deleveraging). Aligns with V8's regime concept: gate admissions by volatility regime rather than by instrument identity.

strategy_name: Session pivot-point support/resistance
mechanism: The prior session's high/low/close average defines objective price levels where the next session's price tends to meet support/resistance; objective calculation makes levels self-fulfilling
setup_summary: Compute pivot = (prior period H + L + C)/3 and three derived support/resistance levels; in the following session fade touches of S1/R1/S2/R2 in a ranging regime (book shows USD/CHF meeting resistance exactly at Support-2); a clean pass through all levels signals unusually strong sentiment - trade with, not against, the break.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: touch of a pivot-derived level. Invalidation: clean close through the level set (trend day) - the book frames level breaks as strong-sentiment signals, so the level trade must be abandoned on a decisive breach.
risk_geometry: Entry: limit at the pivot level; stop: beyond the level; target: next pivot level; expiry: end of the trading session - levels are session-scoped.
quote: A pivot point is simply the average of a currency pair's high, low, and closing prices for a given period of time (typically one 24-hour trading session)... since pivot points are calculated objectively, they will appear the same on all charts and may thus become self-fulfilling.
chapter_anchor: Ch.6 'Pivot Points' pp.143-144
notes: 24/7 crypto has no natural session boundary; requires a fixed rolling window (e.g., 00:00 UTC or 08:00 UTC daily) to define H/L/C. Self-fulfilling-objectivity argument applies equally to BTC (daily pivots are widely published). Candidate behavior family within a location-based reversal mechanism.
book: Forex for Beginners - A Comprehensive Guide to Profiting from the Global Currency Markets 2012

strategy_name: E-ratio: volatility-adjusted MFE/MAE entry-edge measurement
mechanism: An entry's edge can be measured directly before building a full system: average maximum favorable excursion divided by average maximum adverse excursion, each normalized by ATR at entry, over a fixed horizon; random entries give ~1.0, and a real entry must exceed 1.0 over the system's intended holding horizon
setup_summary: For each entry signal, compute MFE and MAE over the next N days (E5/E10/E50/E70...), divide each by ATR at entry, average across signals, and take MFE/MAE. Calibration from the book: 30 random coin-flip tests gave E5=1.01, E10=1.005, E50=0.997; a 20-day breakout entry shows E5=0.99/E10=1.0 (below 1 short-term) but E70=1.20; adding the trend filter lifts E70 to 1.33 and E120 to ~1.6.
trigger_invalidation: An entry with E-ratio <= 1.0 over its intended horizon has no edge; an entry whose edge is positive only at horizons mismatching the system's exit is a system-design mismatch.
risk_geometry: No trade geometry - a pre-trade screening/validation statistic; horizon parameter is the key choice (edge must be measured over the actual holding window).
quote: The E-ratio is the average volatility-adjusted MFE divided by the average volatility-adjusted MAE.
chapter_anchor: Ch.5 Trading with an Edge, The Edge Ratio (pp.66-69)
notes: Directly usable in V8's registry/screening pipeline: measure a proposed expert family's E-ratio on BTC 1h over its intended horizon (e.g., trend_pullback's 8-bar expiry -> E8) before formalizing, and to test whether entry edge exists at all. ATR normalization is PIT-safe. Also supports the book's core thesis (Ch.5): entry edge is horizon-specific, and exits should be matched to the horizon where the entry has edge - relevant to V8's risk_geometry design.
book: Way of the Turtle - The Secret Methods that Turned Ordinary People into Legendary Traders 2007

strategy_name: Opening-gap entry and stop rules
mechanism: Gaps reflect overnight supply/demand imbalance; entering immediately at a gapped trigger price is higher-risk because the gap often marks the day's extreme, so confirmation (first-20-minute range resolution) is required, and gapped stops should be re-anchored to the 20-minute extreme.
setup_summary: Four rules, all anchored to a daily session clock: (1) If a trigger is hit by an opening gap, enter only after the instrument trades through its first-20-minute high (longs) / low (shorts) by >=10 cents; ignore gaps under 10 cents. (2) If an open position gaps beyond its stop, hold the first 20 minutes then re-anchor the stop to 10c below the 20-min low (longs) / 10c above the 20-min high (shorts). (3) Gap >=2% in the trade's favor overnight: sell half at the open to lock gains, keep half with a tightened stop. (4) Gap >=2% against overnight: wait 5 minutes, cut if the 5-minute low breaks, else sell into the 9:50-reversal bounce near the 20-minute high.
trigger_invalidation: Failure to break the 20-minute extreme after a gap usually means the gap was the day's extreme - stand aside; rule 4 exists to minimize (not avoid) the loss on adverse gaps.
risk_geometry: entry: 20-minute range break with 10c padding; stop: 20c below morning low (gap-up longs) or re-anchored at 20-min extreme for gapped stops.
quote: ETFs that gap open beyond their trigger prices. For a long setup, buy the ETF only if it subsequently sets a new high after the first 20 minutes of trading.
chapter_anchor: Ch.7 'The Opening-Gap Rules' (rules 1-4; 9:50 a.m. reversal period); applied in Ch.10 DIA short
notes: The rules depend on a daily close-to-open discontinuity and a fixed session clock (20-minute opening range, 9:50 reversal). Crypto perps trade 24/7 with no exchange-level gap, so the trigger mechanism does not exist; perp analogs (funding-induced jumps, weekend session boundaries) are separate phenomena with their own structure.
book: Trading ETFs - Gaining an Edge with Technical Analysis 2nd edition 2012

strategy_name: High-volume doji/spinning top at extremes — supply absorption / exhaustion
mechanism: heavy supply during a decline absorbed by equally aggressive demand (small range on huge volume = absorption); after an extended advance, huge volume meeting the bulls' drive = possible top
setup_summary: After a steep decline into a support area, an unusually high-volume doji or spinning-top bar forms: the high volume proves heavy supply while the small range proves demand absorbed it, increasing the odds of a turn vs a normal-volume session. Mirror: a very high-volume doji/spinning top after an extended advance is a possible top reversal (the bulls' drive met with enough supply to stall).
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: relative volume spike on a doji/small real body at a support area (decline) or after an extended advance. Invalidation: the high-volume bar has a large directional body (no absorption) or price closes through the support area.
risk_geometry: Entry after a confirming candle; stop under the signal bar's low; support reference often anchored to prior pattern lows (e.g., engulfing lows); target not specified in the book.
quote: A very heavy-volume doji or small real body during a steep decline shows that heavy supply is being taken by the equally aggressive demand.
chapter_anchor: Ch 15, 'Integrating High Volume with Spinning Tops or Doji' (pp. 246-247, Exhibit 15.4)
notes: Feeds the DATA_BLOCKED capitulation backlog family (mechanism capitulation_exhaustion). On crypto perps, liquidation-cascade volume spikes make this observable on 1h, but the same spikes can be self-fulfilling; require the absorption (small real body) condition, not volume alone.
book: Japanese Candlestick Charting Techniques 2nd edition 2001 (1)

strategy_name: Trading-range mean-reversion with boundary invalidation
mechanism: range containment breaks are the only thesis killers; reversion to the mean-reversion price/area inside a bounded range is the entry
setup_summary: Define a trading range on the 1h chart from at least two reaction highs (resistance) and two reaction lows (support) plus the mean-reversion price/area (the level price keeps returning to while meandering). When price reverts to the mean-reversion area, enter expecting containment inside the range; the trade thesis is dead the instant price breaks a key support/resistance boundary.
trigger_invalidation: Entry zone = mean-reversion price/area inside the range. Thesis invalidated on a break through the range boundary (support or resistance) - exit immediately regardless of P&L - or when the projected time in the range expires. More touches at a level make it 'stronger'.
risk_geometry: Entry at the mean-reversion price; stop = the adverse range boundary (book: boundaries are 'lines in the sand'); target = the opposite range boundary; expiry = forecast time the range persists (match the option expiry to projected range duration).
quote: As soon as the price action proves the forecast for a directionless market to be incorrect by breaking through a key support or resistance level, one needs to exit the trade.
chapter_anchor: Chapter 5, 'Butterflies and Condors', 'Managing Risk and Taking Losses' (p. 153)
notes: BTC 1h exhibits persistent bounded ranges and mean-reversion behavior; 24/7 trading means boundary breaks are clean close-bar signals with no closed-market gaps. Edge claim unproven - needs OOS falsification. Book profits the range via long butterfly/condor (short-vol wrapper with hard risk limit), which is not perp-executable, but the range-identification and invalidation framework transfers directly.
book: Option Spread Strategies - Trading Up, Down, and Sideways Markets 2009

strategy_name: Synthetic-equivalency relative-value arbitrage (box / jelly roll) as basis analog
mechanism: synthetically equivalent exposures must price to the same fair value; persistent deviation reveals a relative-value edge that converges at expiry
setup_summary: Relative-value methodology: the long box (bull call spread + bear put spread, same strikes/expiry) has zero Greeks and a maturity value of the strike differential discounted by carry, so call-spread value + put-spread value must equal box value; the jelly roll anchors call vs put time spreads to a carry differential. 'If the equation does not balance, there is a relative advantage available' - pick the cheap synthetic for entry or exit. Perp analog: perp-vs-spot basis and funding deviations from fair value create cash-and-carry / basis convergence trades.
trigger_invalidation: Enter only when the identity (CS+PS=BOX; CTS-PTS=JR) is out of balance beyond execution costs; exit on convergence to fair value. Execution costs (commissions, wide ITM spreads) can erase the edge.
risk_geometry: Market-neutral structure with zero delta/gamma/vega/theta; risk = carry, execution cost, and expiry handling; needs spot+perp data (DATA_BLOCKED until derivatives tape in V8).
quote: Remember that call spread value + put spread value = box value. If the equation does not balance, there is a relative advantage available.
chapter_anchor: Chapter 2, 'Verticals', 'Practical Uses' (p. 54)
notes: The box/jelly-roll identities are the equity-option form of the perp basis/carry identity (funding_present_value + spot = perp). For V8 this is a backlog family gated on the derivatives tape; the methodology lesson (relative-value entry/exit selection) transfers even before the tape exists as an execution principle.
book: Option Spread Strategies - Trading Up, Down, and Sideways Markets 2009

strategy_name: Expectation/Edge Metric (E = PW·AW − PL·AL)
mechanism: Win rate is near-meaningless; edge is driven by the magnitude asymmetry of winners vs losers, so a low-win-rate system can have a far higher per-trade expectation than a high-win-rate one.
setup_summary: Evaluate any V8 expert by edge E = (PW × AW) − (PL × AL). The book's data shows Turtle-style trend traders (35-40% winners, expectation 0.81-2.83 monthly) beat buy-and-hold index expectations (0.60-0.93). A system with 40% winners and $1000 avg win / $350 avg loss has edge $190 vs $75 for a 50%-winner system.
trigger_invalidation: E > 0 required to trade; E is recomputed on frozen OOS per V8's learning protocol. Percent accuracy alone must never gate an expert.
risk_geometry: Evaluation metric, not a trade geometry.
quote: Edge = (PW × AW) − (PL × AL) ... The second trading system's 'edge' is 2.5 times that of the first even though it has a much lower winning percent. ... Percent accuracy means nothing.
chapter_anchor: Ch. 5 'The Rules', Expectation (pp. 68-70)
notes: Adopt E as the canonical per-trade metric for V8 registry/screening decisions (alongside drawdown and risk-of-ruin), replacing win-rate heuristics. The Turtle-vs-index expectation tables are a falsifiable empirical exhibit that magnitude asymmetry, not accuracy, is the driver.
book: The Complete Turtle Trader - The Legend, the Lessons, the Results 2007

strategy_name: Mean Reversion Tail Risk (LTCM/Amaranth caution)
mechanism: Mean-reversion/arbitrage strategies are right most of the time and then suffer a fat-tail event where the market refuses to revert, wiping out years of small wins (LTCM 1998, Amaranth 2006).
setup_summary: Caution against mean-reversion families: 'mean reversion works almost all of the time, then it stops and you're out of business.' Trend following accepts many small losses to be present for the rare large trend; Dennis/Turtles were net winners in August 1998 while LTCM imploded.
trigger_invalidation: Not a trade rule but a family-level gate: any mean-reversion expert must be stress-tested on regimes where the reversion thesis fails (trending/cascading markets), and sized so the failure scenario is survivable.
risk_geometry: None — portfolio/philosophy-level constraint on which mechanism families V8 should prioritize.
quote: Mean reversion works almost all of the time. Then it stops and you're kind of out of business. The market is always reverting to the mean except when it doesn't.
chapter_anchor: Ch. 11 'Seizing Opportunity', Hedge Fund Blowups (p. 164)
notes: Crypto perps are prone to funding-driven mean reversion with violent deleveraging cascades; this lesson argues for gating any mean-reversion family on tail-risk survival. Supports V8's trend-following orientation without claiming edge.
book: The Complete Turtle Trader - The Legend, the Lessons, the Results 2007

strategy_name: COT Index commercial extreme setup
mechanism: Hedgers are negative-feedback traders who scale-buy weakness and scale-sell strength; when their normalized net position reaches a historic extreme (percentile of a rolling look-back range), the move that carried them there is exhausted and a reversal setup forms.
setup_summary: Weekly: compute the percentile rank of the commercial (or counterparty) net position within a rolling look-back (book default 36 months, %K-stochastics formula on net positions instead of price). Reading >=90% = commercial buying climax = long setup; <=5% = commercial selling climax = short setup. The extreme alone is not an entry: pair it with a technical breakout-type trigger plus an overriding risk filter (the pattern used by the fund manager Briese profiles, unchanged for 15 years).
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: COT Index crosses the 90%/5% threshold; signal is only valid if the trend resumes after it. Invalidation: the extreme fails to produce follow-through - COT buy signals routinely fail in bear markets and sell signals are premature in bull markets, and such failures CONFIRM the prevailing trend rather than reverse it.
risk_geometry: No stop/target stated in the book. Entry is on trend-resumption confirmation, not at the extreme; cited academic work (Wang 2001) found signals profitable out to ~8-week holding periods; commercial extremes are positioned as setups, with the technical trigger supplying the actual entry.
quote: A 90 percent COT reading suggests a commercial buying climax; a 5 percent reading implies an imminent commercial selling climax.
chapter_anchor: Ch 6, The COT Index, pp. 63-73; Preface pp. xxi-xxiv
notes: No CFTC-style commercial/speculator segmentation exists for crypto. A funding-rate or OI percentile could proxy the 'positioning extreme', but the smart-money-vs-crowd split is not directly observable, so V8 needs a formalized crypto positioning proxy before this family can be coded. Wang 2001 (buy spec sentiment >80% + fade hedger sentiment <20%) is the empirical anchor, annualized 18.9-43.8% across 2-8 week holds.
book: The Commitments of Traders Bible - How To Profit from Insider Market Intelligence 2008

strategy_name: Seasonal hedging composites (rejected scheme)
mechanism: Claim: comparing current hedging to the multi-year seasonal average of commercial hedging reveals whether commercials are more or less bullish than usual. Verdict: the seasonal composite is a smoothing artifact - year-to-year variance swamps the mean, so deviations from the 'seasonal average' carry no forecast value.
setup_summary: Rejected practice: average weekly net commercial positions by calendar week across years (easy to sum and divide) and compare the current year's hedging against that 'seasonal norm'. The book shows the annual lines scatter wildly around the composite (corn example: short hedging peaks at week 11, long hedging at week 40 on average, but individual years diverge massively), so a current-year deviation is not statistically meaningful.
trigger_invalidation: n/a - rejected; the test the author applied was whether a statistically reliable seasonal bias exists (it does not).
risk_geometry: n/a
quote: To be of any help, there would need to be a statistically reliable seasonal bias. I have done the math; it is not there.
chapter_anchor: Ch 4, pp. 43-45 (Seasonal vs Actual Graph of Commercial Hedging)
notes: No crop cycle in crypto; the transferable lesson is a caution against calendar-averaging ANY positioning/funding series and reading deviations as signal without a variance test - directly relevant to any time-of-day or funding-cyclicality feature V8 may propose.
book: The Commitments of Traders Bible - How To Profit from Insider Market Intelligence 2008

strategy_name: Stochastic Normalization of Net Positions (COT Index)
mechanism: ranking a trader-group net position within its historical range via the stochastic formula yields a 0-100 gauge that is scale-insensitive to open-interest growth, making positioning comparable across eras
setup_summary: Construct a positioning gauge by ranking the group net position against its historical range (stochastic formula): 0 = most bearish historical extreme, 100 = most bullish. Ratio variants (percent-of-total and percent-of-group) are insensitive to large OI swings from quarterly contract rollovers, unlike the raw subtraction form, which visibly widens during OI surges (Appendix A, Fig. A.2). Look-back period choice changes signal frequency.
trigger_invalidation: N/A — methodology. Caveat: the subtraction form's pattern changes with OI growth; ratios give scale-stable patterns.
risk_geometry: N/A
quote: COT index Based on stochastics, a formula that compares the current net position to its historical range and ranks it on a scale of 0 percent (most bearish) to 100 percent (most bullish).
chapter_anchor: Glossary 'COT index'; Appendix A 'Alternative Net Position Formulas' (Examples 1-5)
notes: The rank-vs-range normalization transfers directly to a funding-rate or long-open-interest gauge in crypto; V8 feature construction should prefer ratio/rank normalization over raw levels.

strategy_name: Intraday zone-touch reversion (preplanned S/R scalping)
mechanism: mean reversion at predefined support/resistance: price touching a mapped zone reverts toward the opposite zone level
setup_summary: Predefine intraday support and resistance levels (in the case study a 7-10 tick range). Buy at support / sell at resistance, target the opposite level, and exit on the rotation to objective. Stop is a fixed 2-3 ticks beyond entry, sized to the assessed reliability of the S/R levels; thesis is invalidated if price trades more than 2-3 ticks through entry.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: price touches a pre-mapped support (LONG) or resistance (SHORT) zone. Invalidation: price trades >2-3 ticks through entry in the adverse direction, or the zone fails to hold.
risk_geometry: Entry: limit-style at the predefined zone (wait for price to hit the level); stop: 2-3 ticks beyond entry (fixed tick, chosen from reliability of the S/R levels); target: opposite zone level; expiry: no explicit bar count — 'wait for the market to rotate' to objective.
quote: The plan was for him to stand in the pit and wait for the price to hit his target (buy support or sell resistance), execute the trade, wait for the market to hit his objective, and then exit the trade. If the market traded through his entry point in the opposite direction by more than two or three ticks, he was supposed to execute the loss without hesitation.
chapter_anchor: Ch. 8, The Three Stages to Becoming a Successful Trader (pp. 67-68, floor-trader case study)
notes: Single case study, not a statistical claim; evidence-class NARRATIVE. Transfer to BTCUSDT 1h is indirect: the pit-session 'rotation within a day' rhythm does not exist in a 24/7 perp, and the 7-10 tick scalping frame is sub-bar at 1h. The falsifiable core (zone-touch reversion with a structurally-sized stop and opposite-zone target) is a candidate mean-reversion family distinct from all currently formalized V8 experts. Coordinate with the sibling part-2 reader: same book may reprise this in Ch. 15 (Psychology of Price Movement).

strategy_name: Stops do not cap worst-case loss (gap/slippage through stop)
mechanism: a stop order caps nominal risk only if price trades through the stop level; gaps/slippage mean realized loss can exceed the stop distance, so risk sizing must price worst-case slippage, not the nominal stop
setup_summary: Risk-model rule: even a disciplined stop does not bound realized loss, because the market can gap through the stop level. The simulator and risk sizing must model worst-case fill beyond the stop, not assume stop-level execution.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: any stop order. Invalidation: a fill assumed exactly at the stop price is a modeling error; worst-case slippage must be a parameter.
risk_geometry: Stops: exit triggered at stop level, filled at the gap-through price (worst-case slippage must be modeled); this is a fill/cost-model rule, not an entry geometry.
quote: You don't ultimately know what your risk is, even if you are disciplined enough to use stops, because the market could gap through your stops.
chapter_anchor: Ch. 8, The Three Stages to Becoming a Successful Trader (p. 61)
notes: In crypto perps there is no exchange-session gap (24/7), but liquidation cascades, thin order books, and mark-vs-last dislocation produce stop-through slippage that is the perp analogue of a gap. Validates V8's canonical L1 simulator's STOP_FIRST + gap/slippage semantics and the Binance USDM cost model; confirms gap semantics must be retained even though 'no exchange gaps' is often claimed.

strategy_name: fomo_cockiness_guard
mechanism: early wins inflate perceived skill and trigger FOMO/oversizing, converting a profitable run into ruin; the two documented failure modes are believing one's own B.S. and the fear of missing out
setup_summary: Behavioral guard: after a short winning streak (the book's exemplar: one $10M winner -> 'I lost on my next 13 trades... a fourteen-million-dollar hole'), position size must stay flat and no discretionary size increase or 'trade the opposite of the signal because it worked once' reversal is allowed. 'Making money on my first trade... was probably the worst thing that I could have done.'
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: consecutive wins or a single outsized win in the account history. Invalidation: any account-level rule cannot invalidate psychology, but the guard lapses only via registry-gated size review after a frozen-OOS sample; there is no market invalidation for this finding.
risk_geometry: No entry/stop/target geometry; the lesson is a cap on notional escalation and a prohibition on signal-reversal trades driven by one prior lucky opposite-side fill.
quote: Rule Number One: Don't Become Cocky... the fear of missing out was the second greatest mistake that I could ever make. And the first? Believing my own B.S... I lost on my next 13 trades. All of them... I got bold when I should have sat on my profits.
chapter_anchor: Ch. 5 p.38-39 (13 losses) and p.44 (napkin rule); Ch. 6 'A Turn for the Worse' p.47-54 (doubling up against the signal at FOMC)
notes: Not directly codifiable as an entry signal, but it motivates two concrete V8 gates: (1) the RiskGate should reject size escalation that is keyed to recent win count, and (2) the registry protocol already prevents an Expert from being 'promoted' on a short win-streak sample — this fable is the canonical cautionary tale for the small-sample gate. FOMO behavior in 24/7 perp markets manifests as chasing momentum after a big candle or doubling after a flush; rule 16 (one exposure per direction) partially neutralizes the revenge-double.

strategy_name: Support/Resistance range fade with stop-and-reverse
mechanism: A repeatedly-tested support/resistance level concentrates opposing expectations; the disappointed side is forced to liquidate, so the edges of a balance area are high-probability fades until one side proves dominance.
setup_summary: In an established trading range (book example: a two-week band between 94-10 and 95-25), place resting orders a few ticks inside each boundary: sell near resistance, buy near support, with a stop-and-reverse order beyond the boundary. The weight of each level grows with the number of failed penetration attempts. On 1h BTCUSDT: a defined high/low zone rejected at least 2-3 times with a similar pullback magnitude each time.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger = price trades into the resting zone at a range edge. Thesis invalidated when price stops-and-reverses through the boundary by the book's ~6-tick margin (the market defines itself by penetrating), converting the fade into a breakout trade in the penetration direction.
risk_geometry: Entry: resting limit orders INSIDE the range edges, not at the exact extreme (early anticipators of the failure sell/buy first and you miss the fill); stop: stop-and-reverse beyond the boundary by a small margin; target: opposite side of the range; no bar expiry stated.
quote: put your orders in a place where the highest probability is that it will continue in the direction of your trade
chapter_anchor: Ch.15 'The Psychology of Price Movement' - Support and Resistance / trading range, pp.160-162
notes: Self-fulfilling-prophecy logic ('All beliefs eventually become self-fulfilling prophecies'): S/R works because enough traders act on it. 24/7 perp crypto has clean level tests (no gaps) but high leverage makes liquidations at range edges push ranges through; needs a range-definition feature (location + history) plus a small-margin reverse trigger.

strategy_name: Buy/sell away from value (balance-area extremes)
mechanism: Most trading activity clusters in a comfort balance area (bell-curve distribution of price-time); trades away from value have the fewest participants because traders fear being alone there, so the extremes of the balance area are where the best opportunities are.
setup_summary: Identify the value/balance area where the majority of trading activity clusters; trade the first departure of price from its edge back toward value. On 1h BTCUSDT: a high-volume cluster zone; enter on the first test beyond the zone's edge, fade back toward the zone interior.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger = price departs from the value-area boundary. Thesis (reversion to value) invalidated if the departure is forceful enough to set off chain reactions - new participants joining the break side and old position-holders liquidating in the break direction.
risk_geometry: Entry: at the departure from the value-area edge; stop: beyond the departure point; target: back into the value area; no expiry stated.
quote: to 'buy or sell away from value'... these are the scariest trades to make because the trader who can make them is all alone; there is no safety in numbers.
chapter_anchor: Ch.15 'Balance Areas', pp.157-158 (citing Steidlmayer & Koy, Markets and Market Logic, 1987)
notes: The book's balance-area concept is the value-area/TPO idea (majority of activity in a bell-curve range) with a psychological twist: traders cluster at 'comfort' (the middle), not fair value. Requires volume-by-price / TPO-style distribution beyond V8's canonical L1 bars; the reversion-to-value trade needs a defined value boundary feature.

strategy_name: 'Stomach 80% full' - correction after ~8-10 consecutive new highs/lows
mechanism: extended runs of record highs/lows without a meaningful correction concentrate longs/shorts and exhaust fuel; after about eight to ten records the odds of a significant correction are strong
setup_summary: Count consecutive 'record highs' (new highs for the move) or 'record lows' without a meaningful correction. After about 8-10 such records the odds are strong that a significant correction will unfold; at 8+ records the Japanese say 'the stomach is 80% full'. The book's gold example: 8 new higher highs reaching a window-resistance area was a double caution (record count + resistance confluence). A meaningful correction resets the count.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: 8-10 consecutive record highs (or lows) with no meaningful correction. Invalidation: a meaningful correction resets the count; a persistent new-leg up past ~10 records (the rule is a probability statement, not a barrier).
risk_geometry: Risk-rule/filter, not an entry: use as a caution signal to trail stops, take profit on longs (or shorts), or gate new long entries near resistance; the book pairs it with resistance confluence (window 2) for stronger tops.
quote: Candlestick theory states that after about eight to ten new highs or lows, without a meaningful correction, the odds are strong that a significant correction will unfold.
chapter_anchor: Ch. 7 'Continuation Patterns - Windows' (Eight New Record Highs, gold example) p.128
notes: Extremely falsifiable counting rule on BTCUSDT 1h: a 'consecutive record count' feature in the history group is trivial to compute PIT, and leveraged crypto trends commonly run 8-10 1h records before violent corrections (funding accumulates). Best mapped as a risk/regime feature (reduce long aggression, raise stop-trail sensitivity) rather than a standalone expert - the book itself presents it as caution confluence, and a correction is not necessarily a reversal.

strategy_name: Candlestick pattern validity by close position within bar range
mechanism: the close's position within the bar's range determines whether a candlestick pattern is valid; the open and early-bar path matter less
setup_summary: A candlestick setup is valid only if the close lands in a specific position: bearish big shadow closes near the low, bullish big shadow closes near the high. Molly's mechanical version: shadow larger than the prior five candlesticks by at least 15% and close within ~15 pips of the extreme; trigger on the next bar; target the nearest zone; three-bar exit.
trigger_invalidation: close outside the required position -> pattern invalid, no signal
risk_geometry: entry: next-bar close; stop: beyond pattern extreme; target: nearest zone; exit: three-bar rule
quote: If the closing price for a bearish big belt is not near the low, but rather near the middle of the candlestick, is it a valid sell signal? The closing price is absolutely critical to the naked trader.
chapter_anchor: Ch 14, A Simple Trick (pp. 236-238); Ch 13 subjectivity example (Molly, pp. 224-225)
notes: Close-position-in-range is computable per bar and consistent with V8's NEXT_BAR_CLOSE trigger semantics; pip-based filters need translation to ATR/volatility units for 1h BTCUSDT. The candlestick-snapshot exercise itself is expertise-building, not a strategy; the load-bearing falsifiable content is the close-position validity rule plus Molly's mechanical filters.

strategy_name: Big Shadow zone-reversal engulfing
mechanism: A zone-printed engulfing candle whose range dwarfs the prior candles signals exhaustion: the market over-extended into a price-memory level and was rejected.
setup_summary: On a support/resistance zone, two candles form a big shadow: the second candle has a higher high and lower low than the first, a wider range than the prior 5-10 candles, and closes near its extreme (bullish close near high, bearish close near low). Best set-ups have 'room to the left' — the market has not printed on the zone for at least 7 candles. Enter via a stop beyond the big-shadow candle; stop a few pips beyond the opposite extreme; target the nearest zone.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: engulfing two-candle formation on a zone with close near the extreme and range > prior candles. Invalidation: stop a few pips beyond the big-shadow candle extreme; set-ups whose close sits near the candle midpoint, or that print where recent price action exists at the zone, are skipped.
risk_geometry: Entry: buy stop a few pips above the big-shadow high (bullish) / sell stop below the low (bearish). Stop: a few pips beyond the opposite extreme of the big-shadow candle. Target: nearest zone (with cushion). Expiry: none stated; 'room to the left' >= 7 bars is the quality gate.
quote: Big shadows must print on the zones. Big shadows print at extreme highs or extreme lows... The very best big-shadow candlesticks have room to the left.
chapter_anchor: Ch.6 'The Big Shadow' pp.95-110 (rules p.109, optimizers p.110)
notes: Distinct from V8's formalized failed_breakout (SHORT reentry below a failed high) — this is a two-candle zone-rejection reversal. The falsifiable differentiators are the close-near-extreme condition and the >=7-bar room-to-the-left filter (an exhaustion gate).

strategy_name: Bollinger-Band Support/Resistance and Band-Width Squeeze
mechanism: Price tends to meet resistance at the +2-sigma band and support at the -2-sigma band around a 20-period MA (95% containment); unusually narrow band width (low volatility) is usually followed by high volatility, so band contraction is a volatility-expansion precursor.
setup_summary: Bollinger bands = 20-period MA with bands two standard deviations above/below. In an uptrend prices hold above the middle line (support) and rallies stall at the upper band; corrections find support at the 20-day line or the lower band. In a downtrend, the 20-day line is resistance and prices bounce off the lower band. Band width (contraction/expansion) tracks volatility: unusually narrow bands usually precede a high-volatility move; unusually wide bands warn of trend slowing or a return to a range. Works on daily, weekly, and monthly charts (20-period scaled to each).
trigger_invalidation: Bands are tendencies, not hard barriers; a strong trend can ride the band. The squeeze signal gives no direction (book leaves resolution unstated).
risk_geometry: Entry near a band on bar close with reversion expectation; target = middle line or opposite band; no explicit stop or expiry stated.
quote: Unusually narrow bands (reflecting low volatility and a quiet market) are usually followed by a period of high volatility
chapter_anchor: Ch.4 'Or Put Bands around It' and 'Band Width Is Important, Too' (pp.87-95)
notes: Band-width squeeze is a natural FEATURE_INPUT for the volatility feature group and a setup precursor for the existing volatility_breakout concept. The book also covers fixed-percentage envelopes (3% around 20-day, 5%/10% around 10-/40-week) as the simpler predecessor.

strategy_name: Bullish percent breadth regime thresholds (BPI + McClellan momentum)
mechanism: the proportion of a market's constituents on buy signals measures internal participation; thresholds separate bull/bear/oversold regimes that single-instrument price cannot show
setup_summary: Compute the percent of universe instruments on buy signals (book: NYSE Bullish Percent Index). Below 50 = bear territory, back above 60 required to confirm bull, below 30 = oversold; sector BPI dispersion identifies the weakest and strongest groups. McClellan oscillator (19/39 EMA cross of net advances) gives short-term breadth momentum. Falsifiable: breadth thresholds separate regimes that price alone does not.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: BPI crosses 50/60/30 thresholds, or 19-EMA breadth crosses 39-EMA. Invalidation: rapid threshold back-crossing (bounding in the 40-60 band).
risk_geometry: Regime gauge only: no entry, stop, target, or expiry stated. Used to filter group participation and confirm 'bear market rallies'.
quote: readings in the NYSE Bullish Percent Index ($BPNYA) well below 50 percent put it in bear market territory; and that a move back over 60 percent was necessary to put it back into a bull market.
chapter_anchor: Appendix A, 'Bullish Percent Indexes' (figs A.4-A.5) and 'McClellan Breadth Indicators' (fig A.6)
notes: Requires an instrument universe (many perp contracts) for breadth; V8 currently runs a single instrument (BTCUSDT 1h), so this is universe-gated, not single-instrument. In perp crypto the closest analog is breadth of a perp basket (e.g., % of top contracts above their own long MA, or funding-weighted breadth), which is a real sentiment/flow input once a multi-instrument tape exists.

strategy_name: Negative-correlation flight-to-safety hedging (bonds/gold vs stocks)
mechanism: in stress, money rotates out of equities into Treasuries and gold, producing persistent negative cross-asset correlation that can hedge or replace equity exposure
setup_summary: During equity market stress, bond ETFs and gold rise as stocks fall; inverse funds mirror the index so a sell signal on the long vehicle is a buy signal on the inverse. Falsifiable: cross-asset correlation between the risky asset and its hedge turns strongly negative in stress regimes and can be traded directly rather than via hedged net exposure.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: risk-off regime where the counter-asset rallies while the risky asset falls. Invalidation: correlation flips positive (flight-to-safety breaks down; central-bank backstop).
risk_geometry: No entry/stop/target given in Part 2; presented as a portfolio-construction and instrument-selection method (mutual fund/ETF rotation), not a per-trade geometry.
quote: During the second half of 2007, bond ETFs rose sharply as stocks fell. So did gold. ... This is because money rotating out of stocks during a period of economic stress usually moves into the relatively safety of Treasuries.
chapter_anchor: Ch 12, 'Using ETFs to Hedge' (figs 12.1, 12.10); also Ch 11 'Inverse Stock Funds' (fig 11.14)
notes: In perp markets there is no need for inverse vehicles - SHORT is native, so the mirror-image trick is moot. The transferable piece is cross-asset correlation as a feature group input (e.g., BTC vs equity index, BTC vs gold, or BTC vs ETH) for regime detection. Out of scope for the single-instrument program; would need multi-asset data feeds.

strategy_name: Session/participation filter - avoid low-activity noise
mechanism: low-participation sessions produce quick but meaningless swings and volatility, so signals generated there are noise, not information
setup_summary: Filter trade consideration to periods with adequate participation; ignore or down-weight moves made in low-volume sessions. The author trades only pit-session data for ES because overnight volume is low and produces 'quick but meaningless swings'. Falsifiable: compare signal quality (forward return given a signal) by participation bucket / hour-of-week.
trigger_invalidation: Filter is admission-side: signals formed in low-participation windows do not trigger entries (or are marked lower-confidence).
risk_geometry: None stated; purely an entry-qualification filter.
quote: I generally only look at pit session data because the volume is so low overnight and there are often quick but meaningless swings and volatility overnight.
chapter_anchor: Ch.8 Robert's Follow-Up on Kerry Szymanski ES trade (p.221)
notes: Crypto is 24/7 with no exchange close, but participation and volatility cluster by UTC session (Asia/Europe/US) and around funding timestamps (00/08/16 UTC), so a time/participation feature group is directly constructible from perp tape (hour-of-week + rolling volume percentile). Not a strategy by itself; feeds feature-group spec.

strategy_name: Time Band / alternate time projection (cycle-based timing)
mechanism: if the market's recent time-cycle rhythm continues, the next high/low is made inside the overlap window of recent cycle ranges
setup_summary: Project the window for a trend high/low as the overlap of recent high-high and low-high cycle ranges (bull) or low-low and high-low ranges (bear), with outliers excluded; Alternate Time Projections at 62/100/162% of prior same-direction swing durations complement it. Used to time exits near price targets (e.g., gold top projected to mid-March 2008, actual high March 17 at the projected price).
trigger_invalidation: Time window is advisory for exit timing only; the book's own example exited a long near a corrective low before the trend resumed - time projections carry no thesis-invalidating power by themselves.
risk_geometry: Exit-window overlay on price targets; no stop or entry semantics.
quote: In a bull trend, the overlap of the recent high-high cycle range and the recent low-high cycle range. If the recent time cycle rhythm continues, the assumption is the next high will be made in the Time Band (overlap) range.
chapter_anchor: Glossary 'Time Band'; Ch.5 (referenced); Ch.8 Cees van Hasselt gold trade (p.216-218)
notes: Cycle counting (H-H/L-L ranges, outlier exclusion) is subjective; 24/7 crypto data removes the session cadence that anchors intraday cycles; and V8 determinism requires any timing feature to be bar-count based, not wall-clock. Defer behind a gated, deterministic reformulation if ever pursued.
