strategy_name: Dynamic Time Strategy: time retracements + alternate time projections + Time Bands
mechanism: Reversals cluster at harmonic proportions of prior sections measured in time units (time retracements, alternate time projections) and at the overlap of recent cycle ranges (Time Bands); several independent time factors inside a narrow window raise the probability of a reversal there, so a trader is prepared in advance for when to expect the turn.
setup_summary: For a potential three-section correction, project (1) time retracements of the prior trend at 38.2/50/61.8/100/162% (simple ABC corrections usually complete in the 38.2-61.8% zone; complex corrections by the 100% time retracement), (2) alternate time projections of the Wave-A time range at 61.8/100/162% from the B extreme (62% = minimum, 100% = most frequent, 162% = max for a Wave-C), and (3) the recent 100% low-low (or high-high) cycle; the narrow overlap window (+/- 1-2 bars) is the probable correction-completion time. Time Bands: overlap of the recent high-high count range and low-low/low-high count range (5-6 repetitions, outliers trimmed) projected forward.
trigger_invalidation: A new low/high before the 38% time retracement is not a completion (only temporary support/resistance). If price makes a new extreme beyond the 100% time retracement for a complex correction, the time thesis is void (book shows the failed IBM example where the correction high came well after all time factors).
risk_geometry: Time-only readiness tool: no entry or stop of its own; used to be prepared to act on a price-plus-momentum confirmation inside the window. Book repeatedly notes time factors 'warn what is probable and not probable' rather than pinpointing bars.
quote: Most simple three-section, ABC corrections are complete in the 38.2% to 61.8% time retracement zone.
chapter_anchor: Chapter 5, 'Beyond Traditional Cycles' (Time Retracements and Corrections, Alternate Time Projections, The Time Target Zone, Time Bands)
notes: Bar-count projections are fully compatible with V8 determinism (no wall clock; time in bars) and with a 24/7 tape (no session structure to distort counts). Reliability of cycle regularity in high-leverage crypto is questionable - the author himself presents a clean failure - so for V8 this is a 'time' feature-group input (bars-to-window) used as a readiness/regime cue, never a standalone trigger; requires PROJECT_EVIDENCE before any formalization.

strategy_name: Overreaction reversal on discrete news shocks
mechanism: Investors overreact to bad news and react slowly to good news, fixating on the most recent information; the overshoot reverts once the extrapolation exhausts
setup_summary: After a sharp price move on a discrete event (scandal, earnings miss, hack), enter opposite the shock once the recent-information extrapolation has run its course. Exemplar in text: American Express dropped nearly 50% on scandal while the business thesis was intact; the price recovered within ~2 years (author's framing). Falsifiable: shock-overshoot reversal to pre-event level within a defined window.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: large adverse move on an idiosyncratic, news-identifiable event while thesis/conditions are unchanged. Invalidation: the thesis is actually broken (the event changed the fundamentals), so price does not revert.
risk_geometry: Book gives no stops/targets; the AE case held ~2 years and exited on recovery. For V8: bar-close entry after shock, swing/ATR stop, expiry in bars, thesis-invalidation exit via still_valid.
quote: people tend to overreact to bad news and react slowly to good news. Psychologists call this overreaction bias.
chapter_anchor: Ch 11 The Psychology of Money (Overreaction Bias), pp. 184-185
notes: Chapter cites academic behavioral studies (Thaler) for the overreaction regularity. On 24/7 perps news shocks happen intraday and carry no gap protection, so overshoots can be violent and reverts delayed by funding/leverage; the slow-to-good-news half of the claim implies a drift continuation variant worth separating in screening.

strategy_name: Pre-committed invalidation exits against loss aversion
mechanism: Loss aversion is asymmetric (~2x), so humans hold losing positions far too long hoping for a turnaround; mechanical pre-committed exits are the countermeasure
setup_summary: Behavioral claim: investors need roughly twice as much positive to overcome a negative (Thaler experiments), causing them to hold bad choices too long and to defer realizing losses ('the loss doesn't become real until they act on it'). Rule: invalidation exits must be pre-committed and mechanical, not discretionary.
trigger_invalidation: N/A (exit-discipline rule).
risk_geometry: Book gives none; the V8 analog is the dead-thesis (still_valid) exit, which must fire independently of current PnL.
quote: investors feel twice as bad about losing money as they feel good about picking a winner
chapter_anchor: Ch 11 The Psychology of Money (Loss Aversion, Mental Accounting), pp. 185-186
notes: Refines existing lifecycle semantics: V8 already separates stops from dead-thesis exits; this finding supplies the behavioral rationale for why still_valid must be thesis-based and state-frozen, and why holding a loser through funding accrual on leveraged perps is doubly costly (funding + liquidation risk + the psychology the book documents).

strategy_name: Evaluation-frequency myopia
mechanism: More frequent price observation degrades allocation decisions because recent losses loom larger (myopia amplifies loss aversion)
setup_summary: Thaler experiment in the text: subjects shown high-frequency volatile returns allocated 40% to equities; subjects shown only 5-year periodic returns allocated ~70%, same underlying data. Lesson: evaluate performance on long windows and avoid reacting to short drawdown windows.
trigger_invalidation: N/A (evaluation methodology).
risk_geometry: N/A.
quote: The group that had been bombarded by lots of information... allocated only 40 percent of its money to the stock market; the group that received only periodic information allocated almost 70 percent of its portfolio to stocks.
chapter_anchor: Ch 11 The Psychology of Money (Overreaction Bias), pp. 184-185
notes: Corroborates V8's frozen-OOS / long-window evaluation and no-wall-clock determinism: decisions about expert promotion/demotion must be made on the frozen long-window record, never on a live short drawdown. Counterweight against reacting to recent OOS underperformance with in-place parameter changes.

strategy_name: First-N-in-a-group correlated-exposure cap
mechanism: Capping concurrent positions per correlated group prevents correlated losses from stacking into one drawdown event; group-capped diversification beats concentrating risk in fewer correlated instruments.
setup_summary: Group instruments by pairwise correlation (book uses 0.40 as significant); allow at most N concurrent signals per group, bypassing the newest when the group is full. Adding second-tier commodities under first-in-a-group raised gain-to-pain from 4.09 to 5.17; trading one-lot of the augmented basket beat two-lots of the top-tier only (gain-to-pain 7.56 vs 4.09, max DD $17,180 vs $34,568). Large-account version: cap of 7 per group was the optimum (5.36 vs 5.32 baseline).
trigger_invalidation: If correlation regimes shift (groups re-correlate in stress), a static group structure breaks; membership must be computed on frozen windows, not full-sample, or the cap misallocates.
risk_geometry: portfolio-level bypass rule; no per-trade change.
quote: It's better to diversify with second-tier commodities than to double-up on the top-tier set... the gain-to-pain ratio for the augmented portfolio is almost 85 percent higher than the baseline portfolio when trading two lots of the best commodities.
chapter_anchor: Ch.12 'First-N-in-a-Group', pp. 193-196; Ch.14 pp. 224-225
notes: BTC/ETH/alt perps are highly correlated and correlation spikes in stress (the 2008 analog the author describes in Ch.12). V8's one-exposure-per-(instrument,direction) is per-instrument; this extends it to per-correlated-group, a strictly stronger claim worth testing once cross_market feature data exists.

strategy_name: Bundle uncorrelated strategies on combined equity
mechanism: Combining strategies with low-correlated equity curves reduces portfolio drawdown more than it dilutes return because their loss events rarely coincide; diversification credit appears mainly as DD reduction, then as optional leverage.
setup_summary: Run two structurally different strategies (short-term counter-trend Nasdaq scalper + mid-term commodity trend-follower) off one combined equity pot, each at half its standalone risk fraction. 2000-2011: combined gain-to-pain 4.25 vs 2.61 (stock alone) and 2.42 (commodity alone); average annual max DD 6.0% vs 9.0%/11.0%. Best allocation 0.45 commodity / 0.55 stock (4.29); a leverage multiplier 1.0-1.5 scales return 25.3%->39.2% at near-flat gain-to-pain (4.29->4.51).
trigger_invalidation: If the two equity curves become highly correlated (regime convergence), the benefit disappears; the book conditions the edge on strategies being 'different enough' in equity-curve correlation, not just instruments.
risk_geometry: each strategy keeps its own stops/targets; allocation weights sum to 1; optional global leverage multiplier on the fixed-risk base.
quote: The key, of course, is that they need to be different - not necessarily in the instruments they trade, but different enough that the resultant equity curve is not highly correlated with the equity curves of your current systems.
chapter_anchor: Ch.16 'Trading the Stock and Commodity Strategies Together', pp. 241-244
notes: Direct implication for the registry: PROPOSED experts should be screened partly on equity-curve correlation to the 3 ACTIVE experts (max budget, rule 14), and combined-equity (not segregated) allocation halves each strategy's risk fraction. This is a portfolio-level methodology note, not a new Expert.

strategy_name: Correlated-pair divergence reversion (pairs trade)
mechanism: When a persistently correlated pair diverges, short the rising leg and long the falling leg, betting on spread re-convergence; the pair's idiosyncratic spread has bounded variance, keeping risk small and market-neutral.
setup_summary: Select pairs with average Pearson correlation > 0.40 over their lifetime from a liquid universe (~300 pairs from 1,300 stocks); on divergence, sell the rising member and buy the falling member; exit when the spread re-syncs. Development looked good but live trading was disappointing; redeveloped correctly (every pair ever-correlated during its lifetime, not only pairs correlated at sample end) the strategy was 'no longer tradeable'.
trigger_invalidation: The book's own thesis-invalidation: full-sample pair selection is look-ahead curve-fitting - pairs that lost correlation wandered independently and produced mostly losers. Any V8 version must select pairs on frozen out-of-sample windows only.
risk_geometry: entry: both legs market on divergence; exit: on re-convergence; no stated stop/target; author expects small risk from market-neutrality.
quote: When the normally correlated pair started to diverge in price, I'd sell the one going up and buy the one going down, and then wait until they got in sync again and exit with a profit... the strategy was no longer tradeable.
chapter_anchor: Appendix D 'Case 1: Stock Pairs Trading', pp. 273-274
notes: Perps enable clean market-neutral pairs with no short-borrow, but funding on both legs is a carry cost and the selection-bias failure mode is directly reproducible on crypto (e.g., BTC-ETH or index-perp spreads). The primary transferable content is the selection-bias curve-fit lesson; gate any proposal on frozen-OOS pair selection.

strategy_name: Limit-order fill probability and slippage modeling
mechanism: Backtests that assume every resting limit order fills at the limit when price trades through it overstate performance; real fills are partial (~8/10) and fill price is worse than the limit (slippage inside the limit-to-open range).
setup_summary: A long-only stock system entered on pre-open limit orders; backtests kept everything that hit the limit on the open and randomly selected post-open fills. Live trading diverged immediately: only ~8 of 10 open fills (and missing fills were historically the better trades), and fills priced between the limit and the actual open rather than at the limit. 'The hypothetical performance numbers were astronomical.'
trigger_invalidation: Applies only where limit entries exist; V8's canonical fill-at-close L1 is unaffected. If any Expert proposes resting-limit entries, the model must discount fill probability and price fills at worst-of(limit, touch).
risk_geometry: n/a - methodology constraint on the simulator for any limit-entry variant.
quote: My real trading didn't get all the trades that my hypotheticals said I should get on the open, even when price clearly traded below the limit order entry price. I got about 8 out of 10... I'd sometimes get the 99, but mostly I'd get somewhere between 99 and 100.
chapter_anchor: Appendix D 'Case 2: Using Limit Orders on Daily-Bar Stock Data', pp. 274-275
notes: BTC 1h candles routinely wick through levels, so intrabar limit-fill assumptions are the highest-risk fill modeling error. Record as a simulator constraint: keep canonical fill-at-close; if limit entries are ever added, model partial fills + inside-the-range slippage as a documented variant, never assume limit fills.

strategy_name: Focus investing / conviction-scaled big bets
mechanism: concentrating capital into a few high-probability bets, sized by conviction, beats thin diversification because it forces deeper research and lets the highest-conviction edge carry the portfolio
setup_summary: Concentrate rather than diversify thinly: Berkshire put 35% of its common-stock portfolio into Coca-Cola and 40% of the partnership's assets into American Express; more than 75% of holdings are often in five securities. Scale position size up when the probability of success is assessed very high, and down when unsure. Fisher: too many baskets make it impossible to watch all the eggs.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: probability of success assessed at the top of the conviction range. Invalidation: new adverse evidence drops conviction, or the thesis breaks - then exit/trim regardless of price.
risk_geometry: No fixed stop/target; size = f(conviction); entry at attractive price; long holding horizon; concentration is a research-quality mechanism, not a leverage mechanism.
quote: When the probabilities of success are very high, make a big bet.
chapter_anchor: Ch 8 'Value Tenets' - Coca-Cola at 35% of portfolio (p.135); Ch 1 American Express 40% (p.3); Ch 2 Fisher focus (p.19)
notes: For V8: exposure per family/instrument could scale with frozen-OOS evidence strength rather than equal-weight. Caution - interacts with rule 16 (one exposure per instrument-direction) and the heat cap; the lesson is concentration on thesis quality, not leverage. strategy_name: Fear/greed sentiment extreme
mechanism: emotional extremes (fear/greed) push prices far from any fair anchor; the patient side enters against the emotional crowd
setup_summary: When measurable crowd sentiment reaches an extreme (perp funding rate at extreme percentile, long/short ratio, OI/participation blow-offs), price is dislocated and mean-reverts as the emotion fades; multi-day/multi-week horizon on BTCUSDT 1h. Requires a value/anchor estimate to distinguish dislocation from trend.
trigger_invalidation: Extreme alone is insufficient - without an anchor, extremes can persist. Invalidated if the dislocation is fundamentals-driven rather than sentiment-driven.
risk_geometry: Entry on exhaustion signals at the extreme (bar close after a vertical move, funding blow-off); stop beyond the extreme; target reversion to slow anchor; long expiry (bars-to-days).
quote: we simply attempt to be fearful when others are greedy and to be greedy only when others are fearful.
chapter_anchor: Part III opening (1986), pp. 118-119; Part II.A Mr. Market (1987), pp. 64-65
notes: Buffett's version needs an intrinsic-value anchor that perp price data does not have; candidate proxies are funding-rate / OI / long-short positioning (feature groups flow, participation). Backlog until sentiment-derived features exist. Reversion-to-value is NOT price mean-reversion.

strategy_name: Focused high-conviction concentration
mechanism: concentration reduces risk when it raises analysis intensity and conviction thresholds; over-diversification spreads thinking thin and multiplies per-trade costs
setup_summary: Portfolio/expert design rule: maintain a small number of high-conviction, deeply-understood exposures rather than broad diversification; add capital to top-conviction setups instead of the 20th-best idea. Corroborates V8's max-3-active-experts complexity budget, the registry experiment path, and one-exposure-per-direction.
trigger_invalidation: N/A.
risk_geometry: Few positions, large size per conviction, long holding, no forced churn.
quote: a policy of portfolio concentration may well decrease risk if it raises, as it should, both the intensity with which an investor thinks about a business and the comfort-level he must feel with its economic characteristics before buying into it.
chapter_anchor: Part II.C Debunking Standard Dogma (1993), p. 75; Keynes 'few enterprises' letter, p. 81
notes: Conflicts with the statistical-power needs of backtesting (few families = few episodes); for V8 the lesson supports the deliberately narrow expert set rather than diversification-driven family proliferation. Note: arbitrage is the exception requiring wide diversification (p. 78-79).
book: The Essays of Warren Buffett - Lessons for Corporate America 1998

strategy_name: High-volatility entry gate and vol-spike exit
mechanism: volatility clusters; when recent average range is extreme, noise-to-signal is too high for entries and open equity is at risk, so bypass entries above a threshold and exit live trades when the range blows past a limit
setup_summary: Bypass entries when the 20-day average range (scaled to dollars) exceeds a threshold ($700 selected); as an exit, if the 20-day average range exceeds a limit on the close, exit on the next open. On BTCUSDT 1h: gate entries and exits on average true-range relative to price percentile.
trigger_invalidation: Entry bypass when avg-range > threshold; exit trigger when avg-range > limit at close. No independent invalidation - it is a volatility-regime gate, not a thesis condition.
risk_geometry: Exit at next open when triggered; the range filter on commodities cut max drawdown from $354,671 to $86,296 and lifted gain-to-pain 1.23->2.11 (entry gate) then 2.44 (with exit variant).
quote: Table 6.15, which showed that we should bypass entries with a 20-day average range greater than $700. But suppose we enter a trade and things heat up. Maybe the same filter should signal a trade exit if a certain volatility limit is exceeded.
chapter_anchor: Ch. 6, Volatility-Based Filters (Commodities)
notes: Caveat for crypto: volatility spikes often coincide with the largest trends (2017, 2020, 2021), so a naive high-vol exit can cut off the best trades; the book's own low-vol filter and std-dev variants did not help. V8 should test the gate as a distribution-aware percentile (vol relative to its own recent history) rather than an absolute dollar threshold, which does not exist for BTC.
book: Building Reliable Trading Systems - Tradable Strategies That Perform As They Backtest and Meet Your Risk-Reward Goals 2013

strategy_name: Bar-scoring: expected forward return conditioning by criteria bins
mechanism: each bar's profit potential is characterized by binning criteria (e.g., SD of close, SD of volume, range/price, bar type) and assigning each bin its average forward return; the summed score is an expected-value ranking across candidates
setup_summary: For each bar compute several criteria (20-day SD of close position, 20-day SD of volume, 10-day SD of range/price, 8-category bar type), bin each into 20 equal-size bins, and tag each bar with its N-bar forward return (N=2-5). Sum bin-expected-returns into a bar score; trade the top-x scored bars each day (entry next open, exit after N bars). BRAC test showed ~10-15% inherent curve-fit inflation.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: bar score in the top-x of the day. The methodology invalidates if bin separation (top-bin vs bottom-bin expected return) is small - the book's own diagnostic for criterion quality.
risk_geometry: Entry next open; fixed 2-day hold in the developed system; equal-size position = equity/x; 50-trades/day variant returned 47.2%/yr with 18.2% avg of top-20 drawdowns.
quote: Bar-scoring assigns a profit expectation to each bar by using a large set of similar setups and their average return over the expectation period.
chapter_anchor: Ch. 8, Conclusion (Bar-Scoring)
notes: Bar-scoring is cross-sectional (best when there are thousands of instruments); V8 is single-instrument BTCUSDT, so the cross-sectional ranking does not transfer, but the time-series analogue (conditioning 1h bars by SD-of-close, SD-of-volume, range bins and measuring forward expected return) is a direct, falsifiable feature-group study that can inform which feature groups carry predictive signal before any expert is formalized.
book: Building Reliable Trading Systems - Tradable Strategies That Perform As They Backtest and Meet Your Risk-Reward Goals 2013

strategy_name: BRAC test and minimum trade-sample requirements
mechanism: curve-fit severity is proportional to too-few trades in the development sample; standard error of mean profit-per-trade shrinks with sample size, and the BRAC (Build-Rebuild-Compare) test quantifies parameter persistence by withholding the last year, rebuilding with the same selection logic, and comparing
setup_summary: Require many hundreds to thousands of trades in any development sample (the book's gold-file experiment shows standard error ~$200 at 90 trades and still ~$100 at 300 trades on a $32.80 mean trade); after building, withhold the final year, rebuild with identical selection steps, and compare on the withheld period. A moving-average system across 37 commodities passed BRAC with identical parameter picks; the Swiss-franc 1980s fit failed out-of-sample (from $8,500/yr to $1,500/yr).
trigger_invalidation: Not a market rule; a development gate. A candidate system that does not pass BRAC is not tradeable regardless of backtest PnL.
risk_geometry: Development-level: trade counts, standard error bands, and withheld-period comparison replace single-chart 'spectacular' curve fits.
quote: for most trading systems (I won't say all, but I'm thinking all) you need many hundreds to thousands of trades in your back-test to minimize the effects of curve-fitting and gain the confidence that real trading will match the parameters of your back-test
chapter_anchor: Ch. 2, Testing for Curve-Fitting
notes: Directly supports V8's frozen-OOS and registry-gated evolution rules: parameter stability ('the best parameter set doesn't flop around from year to year' once trade counts are high) is the falsifiable claim behind not re-optimizing in place. The book also refutes the '30 trades is enough' myth and warns against out-of-sample-by-withholding as inferior to BRAC (withholding shrinks the dev sample). V8's single BTC 1h tape can reach thousands of trades for fast families but not for slow ones - that asymmetry should gate which families are formalizable at all.
book: Building Reliable Trading Systems - Tradable Strategies That Perform As They Backtest and Meet Your Risk-Reward Goals 2013

strategy_name: Common-factor correlation cap (diversification illusion under one factor)
mechanism: Positions in nominally different instruments that load on a single common factor are not diversified; the factor event hits them all simultaneously, so a 'diversified' book collapses as one position.
setup_summary: RiskGate rule: before admitting a book of positions, aggregate exposure by common factor rather than by instrument count. The 2007 CDO error was treating 100 subprime pools (same floodplain: US home prices) as a diversified portfolio and re-rating 80% of the triple-B pile as triple-A; the perp analog is a multi-alt book that is one BTCUSD-beta position, or a short book that is one liquidation-cascade factor.
trigger_invalidation: Cap rule, not a trade: if correlated exposure under any single factor exceeds the heat cap, admission is denied. Continuously validated; no thesis to invalidate.
risk_geometry: Risk rule only; interacts with the RiskGate heat cap and the ONE exposure per (instrument, direction) lifecycle rule.
quote: By assuming that one pile of subprime mortgage loans wasn't exposed to the same forces as another—that a subprime mortgage bond with loans heavily concentrated in Florida wasn't very much like a subprime mortgage bond more concentrated in California—the engineers created the illusion of security.
chapter_anchor: Chapter 3, 'How Can a Guy Who Can't Speak English Lie?' (CDO/synthetic CDO explanation)
notes: Historically confirmed by the AIG FP failure (insured pools went from 2% to 95% subprime without anyone flagging it). Reuses starter slug correlated_exposure_cap. The rule is the direct precedent for V8's correlated-exposure caps.
book: The Big Short - Inside the Doomsday Machine 2011

strategy_name: Kase DevStops volatility-quantile trailing stop
mechanism: stop distance is set at skew-corrected quantiles of the two-bar true-range distribution so stop-out probability is known in advance and scales with volatility AND its variability
setup_summary: Trailing stop follows the highest high (long) / lowest low (short). Warning line = mean TrueRangeDouble (TRD); Dev1/Dev2/Dev3 = 1 / 2.2 / 3.6 std devs above mean TRD, skew-corrected because range distributions are right-skewed. Dev3 is the permanent emergency stop; Dev2 in choppy regimes; front-end MA crossover defaults which side's stops plot.
trigger_invalidation: Stop-out probabilities from empirical hit-hit tables (most active futures, 150k+ bars): Warn->Dev1 ~80%, Dev1->Dev2 ~80%, Dev2->Dev3 ~70%, Warn->Dev3 ~45%; a stop at the warning line has ~50% noise stop-out probability, at Dev1 ~15%, at Dev2 ~2.5%.
risk_geometry: Trailing; stop at TRD quantiles; risk amount pre-calculable (KaseRevAmounts) so position size = risk budget / stop distance; no target; stop widens with volatility and vol-of-vol; 'logical and predictable' versus swing stops which are logical but not predictable in magnitude.
quote: we use 1, 2.2, and 3.6 standard deviations over the average TRD for Kase DevStops Dev1, 2, and 3
chapter_anchor: Chapter 4, 'Kase DevStops' (pp. 169-177)
notes: Crypto perps trade 24/7 with no overnight gaps, so TrueRange equals the high-low range on most bars; the transferable core is the volatility-quantile stop with a stated stop-out probability plus the hit-hit cascade used for scaling out. In V8 this refines stop_r in risk_geometry: replace a fixed ATR multiple with a volatility-percentile stop.
book: New Frontiers in Technical Analysis - Effective Tools and Strategies for Trading and Investing 2011

strategy_name: Bollinger bandwidth-regime band trade (fade wide, ride narrow)
mechanism: bandwidth regime determines whether a band touch reverts to the mean (wide bands) or precedes a directional break to be ridden (narrow bands)
setup_summary: When bandwidth is above its average (vol expansion), sell the close above the +2sd band and buy the close below the -2sd band, targeting the middle band (mean). When bandwidth is narrow (compression), do NOT fade band touches — instead a close beyond a band signals a new trend direction and the trade is to ride the band while bandwidth expands.
trigger_invalidation: Reversion thesis invalid if price keeps closing beyond the band while bandwidth is expanding; the 'riding' trade is only valid while bandwidth expands from compression.
risk_geometry: Entry: bar close beyond the +/-2sd band (20-period MA, 2sd). Target: the middle band / mean reversion. Book specifies no stop or expiry; implies hold until mean; riding trades held while bandwidth expands (can persist several periods).
quote: wider bands offer better opportunities than narrow bands for a mean reversion trade. Narrow bands are more useful for determining the future direction of trend.
chapter_anchor: Chapter 1, 'Applying the Most Popular Technical Indicators — Bollinger Bands' (pp. 25-28)
notes: The load-bearing lesson is regime-conditioning one indicator's signal (fade vs ride) on a bandwidth state; the narrow-band ride side maps to range_compression / volatility_breakout. Crypto vol-regime switching makes bandwidth a natural regime feature.
book: New Frontiers in Technical Analysis - Effective Tools and Strategies for Trading and Investing 2011

strategy_name: Coiling breakout from a narrowing value range (Dynamic VAP)
mechanism: progressively narrowing Unfair-High/Unfair-Low value ranges compress volatility; a wide-range bar breaking the top with a near-high close triggers directional expansion through prior low-volume structure
setup_summary: Track a rolling value-range box (Unfair High / POC / Unfair Low) per timeframe. Consecutive narrowing boxes = market coiling (volatility decreasing, approaching horizontal development); wider boxes = volatility increasing (watch for trend exhaustion). On BTCUSDT 1h, a breakout occurs when price closes above the Unfair High (below Unfair Low) with a wide-range bar closing near its extreme; long entries on the 15m retest at the 15m box bottom (provided price stays >= POC of the VAP map).
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: close beyond the value-range boundary with an expanding bar after a period of narrowing ranges, and 8+ consecutively higher boxes followed by a pause box. Invalidation: close back inside the value range (breakdown of the breakout); failure to accelerate through a hole / prior POC zone.
risk_geometry: Entry on the breakout bar close or the 15m retest; initial stop just below the top of the daily value range (tight), moved up via the 60m as price advances; targets = prior POCs to the left; exit when a new consolidating box forms at a prior POC (supply absorption).
quote: The narrower the price range between an Unfair High and an Unfair Low--and the tighter the area of support and resistance--the more coiled the market is becoming.
chapter_anchor: Ch5 (pp. 265-267) 'Refining Market Analysis and Trading Using TAS PRO Dynamic VAP'; Trading Application #2 (pp. 278-280, S&P e-mini)
notes: The coiling concept is directly computable on 1h BTCUSDT (rolling value-range width percentile as a volatility feature) and the stop/target scheme (below box top, prior POCs) is PIT-safe. Maps to the range_compression strategy slug; candidate new expert family (volatility compression breakout) distinct from trend_pullback.
book: New Frontiers in Technical Analysis - Effective Tools and Strategies for Trading and Investing 2011

strategy_name: Volatility-band stop placement (ATM Trade Velocity)
mechanism: initial stops must sit outside the market's near-term volatility distribution, otherwise normal oscillation stops them out; profit/risk are quantified over fixed horizons (risk ~8 bars, profit ~34 bars)
setup_summary: At entry, project a volatility funnel (standard-deviation confidence lines drawn outward from the entry, based on current volatility). Do not place initial stops inside the 1-2 standard-deviation band - price can and often does trade within it. Expect price to reach the projected profit line; if price hangs below the profit line over time, the position is weak (reduce/exit); above the strong line, consider adding.
trigger_invalidation: Rule applies at entry and during management; a stop placed within the band is mislocated, not a trade trigger. The underlying position logic is invalidated by time (no progress to the profit line within the projected horizon).
risk_geometry: Initial risk quantified over ~8 bars; profit expected over ~34 bars; stop outside the vol band (>=2 std dev), trail as the trade matures; distinct from a fixed ATR multiple in that it is distribution-based.
quote: Be sure you don't place initial stops within these two areas, as price can and often does trade within it.
chapter_anchor: Ch6 (pp. 304-305) 'ATM Trade Velocity', Figure 6.16
notes: Refines V8's stop_distance_atr / atr_stop concept: instead of a fixed ATR multiple, the stop distance is set to the 2-sigma band of a volatility forecast, which is directly computable on perp data (and leverage-appropriate). Candidate RiskGate admission check for existing experts' risk_geometry.
book: New Frontiers in Technical Analysis - Effective Tools and Strategies for Trading and Investing 2011

strategy_name: Range balance fading (buy pivot lows / short pivot highs)
mechanism: in a balanced (supply-constrained) market, fading the range extremes with a higher-timeframe bias captures rotation back toward the opposite extreme; the HVA acts as a magnet in balance
setup_summary: Define a sideways range (>=2 relatively equal pivot highs and lows). Long only at range pivot lows with a higher-timeframe long bias; short only at range pivot highs with a higher-timeframe short bias (or both if undecided). In a mature balance, fade tests of the HVA favoring the POC side (long above POC, short below POC). In early-stage balance, fade only first or second tests of new range extremes (needs supporting confluences/divergences); do not trade the middle of a developing balance - most random, highest noise.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: price reaches a range extreme / HVA test. Invalidation: the extreme breaks (range expansion) - stop beyond the extreme; a transition to vertical phase kills the fade premise (the HVA 'magnet' begins repelling price).
risk_geometry: Entry at range extremes / HVA tests (fade); stop beyond the opposite extreme of the HVA (or beyond the range extreme for early balance); first target = opposite extreme of the balance/range; beyond-range targets only in anticipation of a phase transition.
quote: We trade sideways, nontrending markets as follows: Long: Buy only the price pivot lows of the range if you have a higher-timeframe long bias. Short: Sell/short only the price pivot highs of the range if you have a higher-timeframe short bias.
chapter_anchor: Ch5 (pp. 224-226, 271-275) 'Trading Horizontal Markets', 'Mature Balance Trades', 'Early Stage Balance Trades', Figure 5.6
notes: A complete range-fading spec for the mean_reversion_band slug: HTF-bias filtering, mature-vs-early balance maturity distinction, first/second-test fade rule, and the 'no middle of developing balance' rule. MEDIUM for perps because ranges break violently under funding/liquidation cascades; the HTF-bias and maturity filters are the load-bearing parts.
book: New Frontiers in Technical Analysis - Effective Tools and Strategies for Trading and Investing 2011

strategy_name: Pivot Support-2 reversal (buy near S2, target R1)
mechanism: Pivot-derived support/resistance levels are the market's equilibrium reference; a multi-day decline into an oversold condition at the Support-2 level reverts toward Resistance-1, and price reversion toward the pivot is the causal bet.
setup_summary: After a multi-day decline (the book's example: 5 days down) with an oversold oscillator (daily stochastics %K=66/%D=75 in example, described as 'oversold'), place a limit buy near the pivot-derived Support-2 level; stop below S2 at a fixed price distance; target Resistance-1 / just below the prior day's high; move the stop to breakeven once price advances a defined amount. Falsifiable on any timeframe with pivot levels computed from prior OHLC.
trigger_invalidation: Invalidated if price closes through Support-2 (stop below S2); after a favorable move the stop is moved to breakeven, so thesis dead if price returns to entry.
risk_geometry: Entry: limit order at S2; stop: fixed price distance below S2 (10 points in the bond example); target: R1 (structure); breakeven stop after favorable move; short-horizon expiry (intraday/swing).
quote: Look to buy near Support 2 since the primary support is projected to be lower than the previous day's low... Risk ten points... Profit objective: Look to sell near 101-10 (near today's price from Resistance 1 and below yesterday's high...).
chapter_anchor: Chapter 11, Fig. 11.1 daily trade worksheet (p.195)
notes: Pivot levels computed from rolling OHLC anchor cleanly on 24/7 perps (no exchange gaps), so S2 tags are mechanical. But 24/7 flow plus funding and leverage raise adverse-excursion risk at support, and the book's 'oversold' trigger is loose. Candidate family requires location features (pivot S1/S2/R1/R2) in marketstate; bars-anchored pivot window is a variant question.
book: A Complete Guide to Technical Trading Tactics - How to Profit Using Pivot Points, Candlesticks & Other Indicators 2004

strategy_name: Close-confirmed entry/exit (stop-close-only basis)
mechanism: Requiring the closing range (not an intrabar tick) to breach a level filters whipsaw by making the market 'prove' the move on the close before acting.
setup_summary: Use stop-close-only semantics: exit only if the closing price/range breaches the stop level, and enter only if the market closes above/below a defined point. The book flags the danger: price can close well beyond the intended level, so adverse excursion is larger on the close.
trigger_invalidation: N/A - an execution-basis rule; closes beyond the level are accepted with adverse-excursion cost.
risk_geometry: Trigger evaluated at bar close (final range); entry/exit price may be far from the level on volatile closes.
quote: This is a specific order that some traders use to make the market prove they are wrong when exiting a trade. It can also be used for entering a trade if the market is closing above or below a certain point.
chapter_anchor: Chapter 10, 'Stop Close Only' (pp.181-182)
notes: Direct corroboration of V8's NEXT_BAR_CLOSE entry convention (close-confirmed trigger) and of close-based dead-thesis checks: the market must prove on the bar close, not on an intrabar tick. The adverse-excursion caveat is a simulator-model note (close basis can fill far from the trigger level in volatile bars).
book: A Complete Guide to Technical Trading Tactics - How to Profit Using Pivot Points, Candlesticks & Other Indicators 2004

strategy_name: Leverage fragility / empty-sack risk gate
mechanism: Extreme financial leverage converts a sound position into a fragile one; levered structures profit in booms but are destroyed in adversity, so the leveraged operator's 'easy success' is not evidence of a good business.
setup_summary: RiskGate rule: reject or scale down any CandidateDraft whose effective leverage (notional/margin) or stop distance relative to liquidation price breaches a fragility cap. In the simulator, forced-deleveraging and liquidation cascades must be modeled as real costs, not ignored as tail events. Falsifiable: compare net OOS results of an expert family with vs. without the leverage cap at identical gross setups.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger = candidate leverage or liquidation-proximity above the fragility cap; thesis-invalidation = a position whose margin is so thin that a normal ATR-sized adverse move forces liquidation is structurally rejected regardless of setup quality.
risk_geometry: Entry/sizing rule, not a price geometry: stop distance must clear the liquidation price with margin, else no entry; heat cap per (instrument, direction) tightened when volatility is elevated.
quote: It is hard for an empty sack to stand upright.
chapter_anchor: Part IV.C Leveraged Buyouts, p.149 (Wesco letter, C.T. Munger)
notes: The LBO discussion shows leverage-based gains are mostly tax/reshuffling effects plus a long-boom beta, not acquisition skill ('easy success in such transactions does not imply that success is easy in ordinary corporate acquisitions'). For perps the analog is explicit: leverage multiplies funding and liquidation fragility; a backtest family must be gated so leverage cannot manufacture apparent edge. Refines V8's existing heat cap in src/v8/risk.py.
book: The Essays of Warren Buffett - Lessons for Corporate America 1998

strategy_name: Crisis Dislocation Buying (buy when forced sellers are price-insensitive)
mechanism: forced sellers (margin calls, redemptions, panic, 'the electronic herd') sell regardless of price, pushing price far below value; the buyer with dry powder captures the reversion when selling exhausts
setup_summary: After a violent forced-selling dislocation, buy while the market is paralyzed and hold for reversion: 1974 equities, 2002 junk bonds at 35-40% YTM (back to 6% in 18 months), Feb-2008 auction-rate munis at 10% yields (back to 4%), Korean stocks at 3x earnings. In perp crypto this maps to buying after liquidation cascades / deeply negative funding flushes where price has overshot; 'any calls you get on Sunday, you're going to make money' - seriously distressed sellers signal the opportunity.
trigger_invalidation: Dislocation persists and never reverts because the underlying thesis was genuinely broken (credit/default event, not a liquidity event) - the muni episode was a liquidity dislocation, the subprime collapse was both, and Buffett refuses to catch a fundamentally broken asset.
risk_geometry: Buy only where price is dramatically below a frozen value estimate; no fixed stop given - the margin of safety is the protection; the constraint is having dry powder at the moment of panic (Berkshire keeps a minimum cash reserve).
quote: The key is to buy when others are paralyzed. Stocks in 1974. Junk bonds in 2002.
chapter_anchor: 2006 'Opportunity Cost'; 2008 'Municipal Bond Dislocations'; 2005 'Hair Trigger'
notes: Strongly corroborates the existing liquidity_sweep_reclaim family and the backlogged capitulation family; proposes behavior_family_candidate cascade_exhaustion_buy (mechanism forced_selling_dislocation) as a lower-frequency variant: buy the flush once the forced seller is exhausted rather than the wick-reclaim form.
book: University of Berkshire Hathaway - 30 Years of Lessons Learned from Warren Buffett & Charlie Munger at the Annual Shareholders Meeting 2017

strategy_name: The Past Is Not Prologue - Anti-Extrapolation of Historical Statistics
mechanism: historical statistics, especially recent historical performance, are a weak basis for projecting future edge because the conditions that produced them do not persist; reliance on the past rewards correlation, not causation
setup_summary: 'If investors only had to study the past, the richest people would be librarians.' 'The danger of relying on historical statistics or formulas is that you end up betting on a 14-year-old horse with a great record but now ready for the glue factory.' Munger: 'It's stupid the way we extrapolate the past. Not just stupid, massively stupid.' For a research program: a backtested edge is a hypothesis, not a fact - it must survive frozen out-of-sample and regime change, and the recent past is the least reliable window to project from.
trigger_invalidation: Not an episodic setup; it is the discipline that any in-sample-validated pattern be treated as provisional until it survives frozen OOS and an unseen regime.
risk_geometry: None - this is an evaluation-protocol constraint, not a trade geometry.
quote: If investors only had to study the past, the richest people would be librarians.
chapter_anchor: 1989 'Past Is Not Necessarily Prologue'; 1993 'Value Investing: A Mispriced Gamble'; 2001 'Extrapolating the Past: Massively Stupid'
notes: Fully consistent with V8's evidence-bound constitution: frozen OOS, challenger-versus-frozen-baseline evolution, no in-place learning. Methodological support for treating any backtested edge as falsifiable, and for discounting extrapolations of the recent bull/bear window.
book: University of Berkshire Hathaway - 30 Years of Lessons Learned from Warren Buffett & Charlie Munger at the Annual Shareholders Meeting 2017

strategy_name: Relative-value convergence arbitrage (snap trade / spread reversion)
mechanism: Historically stable relative spreads between two economically linked instruments (futures-vs-bills, on-the-run-vs-off-the-run Treasurys, Italy-vs-swaps) widen to an extreme and then converge; profit comes from the spread normalizing regardless of absolute market direction.
setup_summary: Two linked instruments whose historical spread has widened far beyond its normal range, where a concrete convergence mechanism exists (same issuer, maturity link, or arbitrage relationship). Buy the cheap leg, short the dear leg; position is direction-neutral. Entry on the extreme-widening signal; exit on partial/full normalization or a time bound. LTCM's concrete version: the off-the-run 30y Treasury yielding 12bp more than the on-the-run; $1B long cheap / $1B short dear, held a few months until the spread 'snapped'.
trigger_invalidation: Thesis dies when the convergence mechanism is structurally broken (credit regime change, issuer stress, shift in who holds the paper). Spread widening beyond the entry thesis's stress bound invalidates the holding premise, not just the entry.
risk_geometry: Entry at market on the spread extreme; no conventional stop since the position is held for convergence; real risk is the adverse excursion (spread can go 12bp to 14bp to 20bp) against leverage and margin; expiry is the convergence horizon (months, e.g., the snap trade 'snapped after only a few months'); target is spread normalization, and LTCM 'preferred to reap a sure nickel than to gamble on an uncertain dollar' via ~25x leverage.
quote: the two bonds usually snapped together after only a few months
chapter_anchor: Ch.3 'On the Run', pp.43-45 (also Ch.1 Eckstein futures-vs-bills pp.3-5; Ch.3 Italy-vs-swaps pp.56-59)
notes: LTCM's edge was financing (zero haircut repo) and experience reading models, not unique models ('other Wall Street firms had also found their way to MIT'). No on-the-run/off-the-run analog exists inside a single BTCUSDT perp, so this is data-blocked in V8: it needs a second instrument (perp-vs-spot basis, cross-venue spread, funding-based carry) and the cross_market feature group, which V8 does not yet ingest. The 1998 failure of this exact family is captured in finding 3.
book: When Genius Failed - The Rise and Fall of Long-Term Capital Management 2001

strategy_name: Survival gap for reversion/convergence trades (patient capital vs time-to-convergence)
mechanism: A trade that is 'right' on thesis can still ruin the trader: the adverse excursion can exceed the capital available before the expected reversion arrives. Survival depends on duration-matched capital and funding, not on thesis correctness.
setup_summary: For any mean-reversion expert (pullback_in_trend, band reversion, spread reversion), the time-to-reversion has a wide right tail; episode risk_geometry must set expiry_bars bounded by capital-at-risk and funding durability, not by the thesis. LTCM's design answer - a 3-year investor lockup so it could 'be the bank that could tell depositors, Come back tomorrow' - bought patience, but the August-September 1998 excursion overwhelmed even that capital, so the lockup did not remove the gap.
trigger_invalidation: Thesis-invalidation (still_valid) and capital survival are separate exits: a position can be thesized right and still must be cut when loss exceeds what the book can bear. 'Spreads eventually always came in' was the lesson Meriwether 'could count on' - and the equally valuable lesson he missed until 1998.
risk_geometry: Entry at bar close on the extreme; no tight stop while thesis is intact, but a hard capital-based cut plus an expiry measured in the instrument's convergence horizon; target = normalization. In V8 this means frozen refs + a funded patience budget, not an open-ended hold.
quote: a losing trade may well turn around eventually... but the turn could arrive too late to do the trader any good--meaning, of course, that he might go broke in the interim.
chapter_anchor: Ch.1 'Meriwether', pp.9-10 (Eckstein-affair lesson); lockup design Ch.2 'Hedge Fund', p.27
notes: In crypto perps, funding and vol mean-revert quickly but adverse excursions (liquidation cascades) can exceed a naive expiry; this bounds how long a reversion expert may hold and justifies V8's explicit expiry_bars plus capital-based risk gate rather than thesis-only expiry.
book: When Genius Failed - The Rise and Fall of Long-Term Capital Management 2001

strategy_name: Protective-option hard stop with 50% premium-loss cap and delta-limited hedge coverage
mechanism: A purchased protective option replaces the market-conversion risk of a stop with a fixed-maximum-loss instrument, but the hedge's premium erosion must be capped (50% rule) and its coverage is delta-limited (~0.80) so it is not a perfect substitute
setup_summary: Instead of a stop loss, buy a protective option with a strike at a fixed % loss level (2%/5%/10% of account); the position's maximum loss is bounded by premium plus strike gap, immune to slippage, whipsaw, and gaps. Rule: never let the protective option erode more than 50% of its premium; recognize the hedge covers only ~delta cents per dollar of the adverse underlying move.
trigger_invalidation: Not applicable - risk-structure design.
risk_geometry: Protective strike at ~2-10% loss threshold; erosion cap 50% of premium; delta caps protection (~0.80 even deep in-the-money); leg-out of the losing side converts the protective leg into the new primary position.
quote: The general rule of thumb mentioned in Winning the Trading Game is not to allow a loss of greater than 50 percent of your premium.

strategy_name: Collar: bounded-risk structure that sells premium to fund protection and lock in profits
mechanism: Selling a far OTM option collects premium that offsets the protective option's cost, bounding both loss and profit to a range computable at inception
setup_summary: Long collar: long underlying + buy put near support + sell call near resistance (mirror for short collar). Max profit and max loss are computable at inception; used at trade inception or to lock in profits on a winning trend by rolling the hedge forward. Rules cited: collected premium should be at least ~1/3 of the protective option's potential loss, and the trade should target a 1:2 risk:reward.
trigger_invalidation: If the primary directional trade never develops, the purchased option's time value erodes while you wait; monitor option value (too far vs too close OTM) and expiration vs underlying.
risk_geometry: Protective option at support level; sold OTM option at resistance; profit capped at resistance, loss capped at support minus net premium; sold premium >= 1/3 of protective max loss; 1:2 risk:reward; 50% protective-erosion cap.

strategy_name: Backwardation/contango rotation and cash-futures basis convergence spread
mechanism: When the front month moves to a premium over deferred months (backwardation) or to a discount, the spread mean-reverts as supply/demand and carrying-cost economics normalize
setup_summary: Alert on a market entering backwardation (front month above deferred months): go long front / short deferred to capture narrowing. When it reverts to contango, reverse (short front / long deferred) for the widening. Also trade cash-vs-futures convergence: hold a spot position hedged with futures until the two prices converge at expiration.
trigger_invalidation: If the front contract dips below the back month (discount) on a long spread, cut immediately - a widening spread loses on both sides; persistent backwardation (squeeze) without convergence fails the thesis.
risk_geometry: Pair trade with discounted spread margin; profits from the price difference; exit on discount; unwind triggers new margin requirements; stop-limits recommended because spread trades can lose on both legs simultaneously.

strategy_name: Consolidation/range regime filter (sideways dominance gate on directional experts)
mechanism: Markets spend most time in sideways consolidation; forcing long/short decisions inside a range produces constant reactive whipsaw, so a range regime should suppress or restructure directional entries
setup_summary: Detect a sideways/consolidation regime (book claims ~80% of the time) and use it to gate directional experts: inside a range, trend-following entries are suppressed or must be range-specific (the book's straddle enters both sides on 'sideways + pending announcement'). Range extremes act as support/resistance for the straddle/strangle buy points.
trigger_invalidation: Breakout of the range terminates the consolidation state and re-enables directional setups.
risk_geometry: Range extremes = support/resistance; sideways + announcement is the trigger for both-sides positioning; breakout of range initiates directional entries.
